pages.en:
Simea District.
Incidents during 4-2-72.

Further enquiries by C.B. re m/car 7127 which was brought to the Station 3-2-72. It was ascertained that the car, a Ford Saloon, was the property of "Yu Wha Tang", residing at 200 Route Prosper Paris, French Concession, who, on the 28-1-72, resided at 47 Scott Road. Owing to local disturbances he fled with his chauffeur from above address locking the car in a garage in Sing Yih Foong off Scott Road. The owner was not aware that Japanese had confiscated his car until informed by Police on 4-2-72. The car was returned to him at 4 p.m. 4-2-72.

A Japanese consular official (card attached) together with Teiro Horiba of the Shanghai Cotton Manufacturing Company, Ltd., (card attached) came to Station at 10.30 a.m. 4-2-72 and requested that 7 Japanese subjects detained 3-2-72 be released, stating they would prefer charges against them if they thought fit. Both expressed surprise that Japanese had been kept in detention room in the charge room during their detention. This was explained, the official being informed that other accommodation was not available, and that it would have been inadvisable to have placed them together with the Chinese in the cells. They were escorted to Japanese Consulate by P.S. Fowler and Wilkinson.

At 3.20 p.m. Shih Ngoo Zai, 10 Mei Yue Lee, Avenue Road near Park Road brought to the Station a rifle bullet which had broken a window at above mentioned premises at 3.10 p.m. 4-2-72. It is thought that bullet is Japanese, fired from North Easterly directions.

Curfew being enforced by Uniform Branch 4-2-72, resulted in 2 American citizens, 2 Russians and 106 Chinese being brought to Station between 10 p.m. and 12 midnight, and being detained until and released at 4 a.m. 5-2-72.

During 4-2-72, 2 males were treated at Paulun Hospital and 1 female was detained at St. Elizabeth's Hospital. They were suffering from stabbing and bullet wounds. This brings the total up to 6 a.m. 5-2-72 to 56 persons admitted to hospitals in this district, 2 of whom have died.

Copy to: D.C. Cring,
A.C. Special Branch,
D.D.O. "B".

西摩区。
1932年2月4日期间的事件。

刑事侦缉处就1932年2月3日送至警局的机动车7127号进行了进一步查询。经查实，该车为一辆福特轿车，属居住在法租界霞飞路200号的“余华堂”（音译）所有，此人于1932年1月28日居住在斯科特路47号。由于当地骚乱，他与司机从上述地址逃离，将车锁在斯科特路旁新义丰（音译）的一个车库内。车主直到1932年2月4日警方通知后，才得知其车辆被日本人没收。该车于1932年2月4日下午4时归还给他。

一名日本领事官员（附名片）偕同上海棉纺有限公司（Shanghai Cotton Manufacturing Company, Ltd.）的Teiro Horiba（附名片）于1932年2月4日上午10时30分来到警局，要求释放1932年2月3日被拘留的7名日本籍人士，并表示如果他们认为合适，将对这些人提出指控。两人均对日本人在拘留期间被关押在接待室的拘留室内表示惊讶。对此作了解释，告知该官员没有其他可用设施，且将他们与中国囚犯一起关押在牢房内是不妥当的。他们由警官福勒（Fowler）和威尔金森（Wilkinson）护送至日本领事馆。

下午3时20分，住在爱文义路近公园路梅岳里10号的施五仔（音译）向警局提交了一枚步枪子弹，该子弹于1932年2月4日下午3时10分击碎了上述住所的窗户。据信该子弹为日军所射，来自东北方向。

1932年2月4日，制服科执行宵禁，导致2名美国公民、2名俄国人和106名中国人在晚上10点至午夜12点之间被带至警局，并被拘留至1932年2月5日凌晨4时释放。

1932年2月4日期间，2名男子在宝隆医院接受治疗，1名女子被收容在圣伊丽莎白医院。他们均遭受刺伤和枪伤。截至1932年2月5日上午6时，该区送医人数总计达56人，其中2人死亡。

抄送：副督察 Cring，
特别处助理督察，
“B”处副主管。

pages.en:
Sinza Station.
Incidents during 3-2-32.

Following the Japanese Aerial Observation patrol, between 10
& 11 a.m. 3-2-32, 3 shells fell in Sinza District. One at a Chinese
Dwelling house, 386 Sinza Road, slightly damaging the roof but causing
no injuries. Another at a Chinese dwelling house, 228 East Sz Wen Li,
Tatung Road fell with a like result.

A third landed on the roof of a Foreign Dwelling House, 12
Wong Ka Shew Gardens, occupied by a Mrs. G. Diethelm, a Swiss. It
exploded on impact with a ceiling joist in the Front Attic, 3rd Floor.
Structural damage was slight, being confined to damage of the ceiling.
The Swiss Consul was informed and is anxious to ascertain what force
uses this type of missile in order that the matter may be taken up
to the Consular Body. No body was injured, Mrs. Diethelm, suffering
slightly from shock.

Seven pieces of projectile were found which are being kept for
expert examination.

Inspector Phillips brought to this Station a projectile that
had fallen in the home of a Mrs. Ezra, British, at 696 Avenue Road,
without causing damage or injury. This together with portion of the
shell picked up at Tatung Road, was handed to the U.S.M.C. who have
promised to return same after expert examination.

In all instances the shells appear to be of like make and
judging by the projectile casing of exceedingly cheap manufacture. The
shells appear to have been fired from a N. Easterly direction, but whe-
ther of Japanese origin; or Chinese origin in efforts to hit the Japanese
Aeroplanes cannot at this stage be ascertained.

Curfew:

The Police co-operated with the Uniform Branch in enforcement of
Curfew, and 3 Japanese, 4 Russians and 85 Chinese were brought to Station
The Chinese and Russians were released at 4 a.m. See further report re
Japanese.

At about 10.15 p.m. P.C. 195 Hodgkins brought to Station M/Car 7127,

新闸警局。
1932年2月3日期间的事件。

1932年2月3日上午10时至11时，在日本空中侦察巡逻之后，3枚炮弹落入新闸区。一枚落在中国住宅，新闸路386号，屋顶轻微受损，无人受伤。另一枚落在中国住宅，大通路东斯文里228号，结果类似。

第三枚落在外国人住宅的屋顶上，王家沙花园12号，住户为瑞士籍的G. Diethelm夫人。炮弹在前阁楼三楼撞击天花板横梁时爆炸。结构损坏轻微，仅限于天花板受损。已通知瑞士领事，他急于查明是哪一方使用这种类型的弹药，以便将此事项提交领事团。无人受伤，Diethelm夫人受到轻微惊吓。

发现了七块弹片，正保留以供专家检验。

菲利普斯督察将一枚落入英国籍Ezra夫人家中（爱文义路696号）的炮弹带到本警局，未造成损坏或伤害。这枚炮弹连同在大通路拾获的部分弹壳，已移交给美国海军陆战队，他们承诺在专家检验后归还。

在所有情况下，炮弹似乎均为同一型号，从弹壳判断，制造极其粗糙廉价。炮弹似乎是从东北方向发射的，但究竟是日军所为，还是中方为击中日本飞机而发射，目前阶段尚无法确定。

宵禁：

警方与制服科合作执行宵禁，3名日本人、4名俄国人和85名中国人被带至警局。中国人和俄国人于凌晨4时释放。关于日本人的情况见进一步报告。

晚上约10时15分，195号警员霍奇金斯（Hodgkins）将机动车7127号带至警局，

pages.en:

On searching the car licence papers were found in the name of Yue

With the assistance of French Police, this place was visited and

该车由一名身穿便服的日本人驾驶，向西行驶。

车内有3名日本人和4名俄罗斯人。司机为S. Sasakura，74岁，职业煤炭商，住址四川北路赫伦台（Heron Terrace）74号。他未持有驾驶执照。

他与另外两名日本人T. Yoshiyoko，29岁，职业工程师，住址宜昌路90号，以及M. Imaida，26岁，职业工程师，住址同上，均为布恩路（Boone Road）日本俱乐部的成员，他们称从该处获得车辆。

这些俄罗斯人此前受雇于日本当局，担任司机和装配工，正被送往其在法租界的住所。

1. Eugene. E. Ungenbauer-Ivanow，42岁，职业技工，住址霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）。
2. Anatole Dobrodamoff，35岁，职业司机，住址布尔热瓦路（Rue Bourgeat）682号。
3. Victor Malzeff，22岁，职业司机，住址修女路（Rue des Soeurs）40弄42号。
4. J.S. Sokolovsky，24岁，职业司机，住址法租界霞飞台（Joffre Terrace）112号。

搜查车辆时，发现车牌文件署名为Yue Wha Tung，住址巴黎路（Route Prosper Paris）200号。

在法国警察的协助下，警方探访了该地址，发现此处为“税务学校”，Yue Wha Tung任院长。然而未能找到此人，但秘书称，Yue Wha Tung于1932年1月29日撤离时，将其汽车（牌号7127）留在了斯科特路（Scott Road）新义丰弄（Sing Yih Foong Alleyway）。

全部情况已报告日本领事当局，对方要求将三名日本人扣留至上午8:30以便调查。此要求已获遵从，四名俄罗斯人于凌晨4点释放，除违反宵禁规定外，未对他们提出其他指控。

前三人声称，他们是由香港路6A号的俄罗斯移民协会推荐从事此项工作的，这与所有俄文报纸上警告白俄保持中立的声明直接相悖。

上述陈述将于1932年2月4日进行核实。

pages.en:
The 4th. stated that he had been sent with a letter to a Mr. Ano of
the Japanese Consulate by ex D.S. Podrolivinsky, who in turn sent him
to the Japanese Club where he was engaged as a Chauffeur for $ 4.00 per

Enquiries are proceeding re the owner of the car which is at present

During 3-2-72, 1 male and 1 female were treated at Pavlun Hospital.
(See separate report.) This brings the total to 57 persons, admitted or
treated, two of whom have died.
At about 8 p.m. P.S. Westwood brought to Station one Lieu Tai Foo,

alight. He was questioned and afterwards cautioned and released, being

The District on the whole remains quiet.

J. J. M. Robinson

关于目前扣押在新闸站（Sinza Station）的车辆车主的调查正在进行中。
1932年2月3日期间，有一男一女在宝隆医院（Pavlun Hospital）接受治疗。（见单独报告。）这使得入院或接受治疗的总人数达到57人，其中两人死亡。
晚上8点左右，西伍德警司（P.S. Westwood）将刘太福（Lieu Tai Foo），26岁，湖北籍，职业无业，带至警局。他因在新闸路煽动他人拦截电车和公共汽车并强迫乘客下车而被捕。经讯问后，对其予以警告并释放，经由马克姆路（Markham Road）桥将其送入闸北。
全区总体保持平静。

J. J. M. Robinson
情报官（O.I.）

pages.en:
At 12.35 p.m. a telephone message was received from
Major Bourne that refugees panic stricken by the bombing could
be admitted into the Settlement. They were accordingly
admitted at the Stone Bridge and Wushan Road Bridge, the Police
assisting, in searching the males for concealed weapons.
At 3.15 p.m. further instructions were received that no
more be admitted and the gates were accordingly closed.
Up to 12 m.n., five persons, 1 male and 4 females, are
in hospital suffering from bullet wounds, 3 in St. Elizabeths
Hospital and 2 in FanZao Hospital. Two others were treated
and sent back to their homes.

Particulars as under:
(1) Kyung Ah Ryi, (金阿利), 26, Singpo, 1118 Taitung
Road, s/painter, wounded in calf by stray bullet while standing
on stone road near Wushan Road Bridge.
(2) Wang Wang Su (王汪氏), s/female, Shantung, 21,
Shanghai, wound in right shoulder on Taitung Road.
St. Elizabeth's Hospital.
(3) Tsang Tao Wu (張桃吳) s/female, Canton, 30, Singhai,
wound in back.
(4) Tsang Sung Su (張松氏) s/female, Kiangsu, 40, Singhai,
wound in right thigh and back.
(5) Tsah Tsang Su (蔡張氏), s/female, 30, Singhai,
wound in abdomen, apparently mortal.
No. (2) states that she was deliberately shot by a
Japanese Marine and was escorted by her husband across the
Soochow Creek; he kept watch while in hiding place of safety.
No. (4) is old who came accidentally by the
Wushan Road Bridge when the guard was at its maximum.
Similar stories reported and in general use
concerning the indiscriminate shooting of refugees by the
Japanese Marines and soldiers. Many cases of this
nature have been reported and many more are believed to have
occurred but not reported owing to fear of reprisals.
pages.zh:
下午12:35，接到伯恩少校（Major Bourne）的电话留言，称因轰炸而惊慌失措的难民可获准进入租界。因此，他们在石桥和吴淞路桥被准许进入，警察协助对男性进行搜身，检查是否藏有武器。
下午3:15，收到进一步指示，不再允许进入，因此大门随即关闭。
截至午夜12点，共有五人（一男四女）因枪伤在医院接受治疗，其中三人在圣伊丽莎白医院（St. Elizabeths Hospital），两人在范家宅医院（FanZao Hospital）。另有两人接受治疗后被送回家中。

详情如下：
(1) Kyung Ah Ryi (金阿利)，26岁，新埔（Singpo）人，职业油漆工，住址台东（Taitung）路1118号，在吴淞路桥附近的石路上站立时被流弹击中腿部。
(2) Wang Wang Su (王汪氏)，女性，山东人，30岁，住址上海，在台东路右肩受伤。圣伊丽莎白医院。
(3) Tsang Tao Wu (張桃吳)，女性，广东人，30岁，住址上海，背部受伤。
(4) Tsang Sung Su (張松氏)，女性，江苏人，40岁，住址上海，右大腿和背部受伤。
(5) Tsah Tsang Su (蔡張氏)，女性，30岁，住址上海，腹部受伤，似为致命伤。
第(2)号伤者称，她是被一名日本海军陆战队士兵故意开枪射击的，并由其丈夫护送穿过苏州河；他在隐蔽的安全地点负责望风。
第(4)号伤者是一位老人，在守卫最严密的时候偶然经过吴淞路桥。
有关日本海军陆战队和士兵 indiscriminately（无差别）射杀难民的类似故事广为流传。此类案件已有许多报告，据信还有更多案件因害怕报复而未上报。

Subject (in full) Re Strike in the Yuen Chen Silk Filature, 47 Ferry Road.

Made by D.S.I. Taplin. Forwarded by

Sirs
At 9.30 a.m. 2.11.32 Loh Hai Pao, the owner of the Yuen Chen
Silk Filature which went on strike on the 15.10.32, Mr. Loh in-
formed the undersigned that a "Mr. Tai" ( 戴 ), a representative
of the Bureau of Social Affairs and "Mr. Tsai" ( 崔 ) of the
Shanghai District Kuomintang Headquarters were coming to the fac-
tory for the purpose of settling the dispute between the workers
and the Management. On enquiries being made it was ascertained
that the above presented on behalf of the workers the following
demands:
1. Wages due to them prior to the strike.
2. One month's wages to all employees.
It was ascertained from the owner that he intends to keep
the factory closed for the time being with a view to engaging new
hands. He further stated that they were willing to pay the wages
due to the employees and a further $5.00 to each employee as com-
pensation for closing down the factory. This was not agreed to
by the representatives who then left the factory. The owner stated
that he intended to hand the dispute over to his Lawyer.

（批：1. R. 2.11.32 [签名]）

D.S.I.

[签名]
5.11.32.

诸位先生
1932年11月2日上午9:30，于1932年10月15日罢工的元昌丝厂老板罗海宝（Loh Hai Pao）告知本人，社会局代表“戴先生”（戴）和上海国民党区党部代表“崔先生”（崔）将来厂解决工人与管理层之间的纠纷。经查询，获悉上述代表代表工人提出了以下要求：
1. 支付罢工前拖欠的工资。
2. 向所有员工支付一个月工资。
据老板称，他打算暂时关闭工厂，以便雇佣新员工。他还表示，他们愿意支付欠员工的工资，并额外向每位员工支付5.00美元，作为关闭工厂的补偿。代表们不同意此方案，随即离开工厂。老板称他打算将此纠纷移交给他的律师处理。

Sir:
Re Intelligence Report (Labour) of the 13.9.32 of N. W. K.
Nos.3, 6 & 7 Mills partial Tai-Kung strike and transient strike, I
beg to report that the facts are as follows: that in the past a
number of Chinese clerks who are employed in the offices at the
above numbered mills, were allowed by the management to play foot-
ball on the tennis court in the compound during meal times. A few
days ago they were informed by the management that the Court was
required for tennis and that they could not play foot-ball any
longer. At 12 noon on the 9.9.32 a Japanese employee of the mill
saw the clerks playing on the court and he struck one of them with
a small bamboo cane. The clerks appealed to the Sub-manager on
the 10.9.32 who settled the dispute. The manager stated that no
Tai-Kung strike had taken place with any of the employees in the
above mills.

(毛瑞文) and Tsang Li Sung (張連生).
Conditions in the mill are now normal again.

Stoppage of Work in the N.W.K. No.5 Mill.

At 4.35 p.m. on the 16.6.32 J.D.C.33 reported that a number of em-
ployees had gone on strike at the N.W.K.No.5 Mill, Inspector Jefferson,
the undersigned and a posse of Police attended and from enquiries made,
it was ascertained that a male employee named Sung Hsah Siang (陈玉祥),
age 28 years, native of Shantung, employed as a pump worker in the above
mill for the past eight years, entered the Ring Spinning Room in which
are about 100 machines all driven by electricity, each having its own
1.2
17/6/32 switch and employing about 250 females. After entering this room he
switched off one or two of these machines; this was observed by a Ja-
panese who took him to the Managers office, the reason for this appears
that on the 14th a friend of this man named Wong Tsou Sang (王周生)
who had been employed at the mill for the past 10 years was dismissed
for having caused trouble with the workers and this act was done as a
protest against his dismissal, after these enquiries had been made the
manager decided to dismiss this man also he was offered his pay but re-
fused to take same, however he was escorted off the premises, the ma-
chines were only stopped for about 5 minutes, owing to this special pre-
cautions have been taken to prevent further trouble. Special Branch
informed.

normal this A.M.

1932年6月16日下午4时35分，J.D.C.33（日军指挥部或相关代号）报告称，内外棉株式会社第5厂有部分员工罢工。杰斐逊（Jefferson）巡长、卑职及一队警员到场，经查询获悉，一名名叫陈玉祥（Sung Hsah Siang，音译与中文名对应可能有误，原文拼音Sung Hsah Siang对应中文通常为宋夏祥等，但括号内注明陈玉祥，此处依括号内中文名）的男性员工，年龄28岁，山东籍，在该厂担任泵工已达八年，进入了环锭细纱车间。该车间约有100台机器，均由电力驱动，每台机器均有独立的开关，雇佣女工约250名。进入该车间后，他关闭了其中一两台机器；这一行为被一名日籍人员发现，并将其带至经理办公室。此举的原因似乎是，该男子的一位名叫王周生（Wong Tsou Sang）的朋友，已在该厂工作十年，因引发工人纠纷于14日被解雇，此行为系对其被解雇的抗议。经查询后，经理决定也将此人解雇。虽向其支付工资，但他拒绝领取，随后被护送出厂区。机器仅停运约5分钟。鉴于此，已采取特别预防措施以防止进一步骚乱。已通知特别课。

Intimidation of Mill Workers at the Kim Mills,
      47/49 Nanking Road C.D..

At 11.45 a.m. 31.5.32 three male Chinese ex-employees of the above
mill, names as follows: 1st Lieu Zung Sung, age 38, native of Anhwei,
2nd Lieu Hoo Sung, age 30, native of Kiangsu & 3rd See Dah Sung, age 32,
native of Shanghai, entered the dormitory of the female workers and at-
tempted to prevent them from carrying on with their work, these three
were in possession of bamboo poles. A male Chinese named Lee Kee Dah,
the food contractor for the Chinese female workers and a number of male
Chinese seeing this attacked them striking the 1st named in the neck,
hip and legs, he was taken to the Labourers' Hospital, 48/9 Ferry Road,
where he is at present detained. The Chapei Police of the 6th Division
Nanking Road Sub-Station were called in and are now investigating the
affair.

Mill Situation.

All Japanese and Chinese Mills are working normal this A.M.
The packing coolies, blacksmiths and carpenter in the Kim Mills re-
sumed work this A.M., also the female workers on Night Shift (31.5.32)
show an increase of about 300.

                                  State of District, quiet this A.M.
(Signature)                       (Signature)
Supt. Robertson.

Male Chinese arrested in Possession of
Pamphlets.

    At 2 p.m. on the 25.5.32 P.P.S. Jackson in charge of a Search
Party arrested a male Chinese in possession of a quantity of Pamphlets
on Robison Road near the Tung Hwa Li, from enquiries made it was ascer-
tained that the male Chinese named Tang Sau Woo, age 29 years, native
of Wuhu, residing at the South Tung Hwa Li, had previously been employ-
ed as a coolie at the Tung Yih Cotton Mill, 10 Hokushan Road, and now
as hawker met one named Ding at 1 p.m. to-day at a teashop on Nanking
Road who gave him the Pamphlets to distribute among workers for which
he paid him $5.00, the pamphlets are opposing the Postal Strike and
issued by the Shanghai Labourers' Union of Shanghai, there being no-
thing inflammatory, the accused was released.

    Special Branch and D. C. "B" Division informed.

Communist Pamphlets.

    A number of various kinds of Communist Pamphlets and small
books were found on Kiaochow Road at 11.30 a.m. on the 25.5.32 opposite
the Great China University, it was also noticed that there were a few
copies in the postal system.

Pamphlets forwarded to Special Branch.

一名持有传单的华籍男子被捕。

    1932年5月25日下午2时，由警长杰克逊（Jackson）率领的搜查队在东华里附近的罗宾森路（Robison Road）逮捕了一名持有大量传单的华籍男子。经查询查明，该华籍男子名为唐绍武（Tang Sau Woo，音译），29岁，芜湖人，居住在东华里南区，此前曾在北山路10号的同义纱厂担任苦力，现为小贩。他于今日下午1时在南京路的一家茶馆遇到一名姓丁的人，丁给他传单让他在工人中分发，并支付了他5.00美元。这些传单反对邮政罢工，由上海上海劳工联合会发行，因内容并无煽动性，被告已被释放。

N.W.K. Mill No.1 & 2 Mills Suspension of Work.

Reference the suspension of work at the N.W.K. No. 1 - 2 Mills,
68 Robinson Road O.O.L. on the 16.5.32, two male and six female workers
of the night shift were dismissed on the 16.5.32 in connection with the
above suspension of work.

Pamphlets were found in the above mills, translation as follows:-
"Asking the management for a bonus and the withdrawal of the
Italian Marines, further to reinstate the dismissed workers".
Pamphlets forwarded to Special Branch.

Between 12 noon and 1 a.m. 16.5.32 the spinning room workers of
the above mill suspended work, as a demand for an increase in wages
but resumed unconditionally.

30 night shift workers of the weaving shop (N.W.K. 1 & 2 Mills)
entered the mill at 6 p.m. 16.5.32 but did not commence work until 11
p.m. reason for this was apprehension that the workers would be met
because they thought they would be interfered with by the soldiers
who were dismissed on the morning of the 16th (2 female & 8 male).

Distributing of Pamphlets.

At 4.30 p.m. this inst. 10.5.32 C.P.C. 28 on duty at Robison and
Kiaochow Roads reported by phone that a dark blue M/Car No.3992 had
just passed him on Robison Road proceeding from West to East, the car
was occupied by the chauffoir and one occupant who threw out from the
car a number of pamphlets issued by the Shanghai District Merchants'
Self-Relief Federation. Pamphlets forwarded to Special Branch.
（批：P.P. 11/5/32 / R.W.）

From enquiries at the Traffic Office the car is registered in the
name of C. Kato, 13 Horrioka Road. A search was made of the District
but the car was not located, message circulated to C.C.R.

Refugee Camp O.O.L. 415 (Unoccupied houses).

Communistic Slogans.

At 10 a.m. 9th inst. slogans "Down with Japan", "Demands increase
of Wages", "Return the Settlement and Celebrate the Victory", were
found chalked on the walls on West Soochow Road, near the Foh Yih
Cotton Mill and Ichang Road, near Ferry Road.
Washed off immediately.

Communistic Pamphlets.

At 9.05 p.m. 9th inst, a few pamphlets of a kind which are issued
by the "Western District Mill Workers Association", Anti-Japanese and
Communist were thrown on the ground outside the Sung Sing No.2 Cot-
ton Mill, Ichang Road, by an unknown male Chinese who mixed with the
crowd at the front gate.

At 9.30 p.m. 9th inst, C.P.C.H45 brought to the station from
Ichang Road near Fung Hwa Li, several pamphlets of the same kind as
the above report, which he found on the roads, these had evidently
been dropped by some person on seeing the Police.

At 10.30 p.m. 9th inst., C.P.C's 2061 and 2012 brought to the station
several Communistic pamphlets which were found on a vacant
lot near the corner of the Fung Hwa Li at 10.30 p.m. 9th inst,
similar to those in previous reports.

All forwarded to Special Branch.

Mill Situation.

All the Japanese and Chinese Mills in this District are working
full time, except.

State of District, quiet this A.M.

本月9日晚上10时30分，华捕2061号和2012号将数份共产主义传单带至巡捕房，这些传单是于本月9日晚上10时30分在凤华里拐角附近的一块空地上发现的，与此前报告中所述的传单类似。

Male Chinese Wounded by Japanese Marines in Chapei.

At 6.30 p.m. on the 7.5.32 a telephone message was received from
C.P.C.1756 to the effect that a male Chinese was lying sick on the
N.W.K. No.5 Mill Jetty West Soochow Road. From enquiries made it was
ascertained that a coolie named Wang Fuh Loong (王福龍), age 38,
native of Kiangsu and residing in Chapei, whilst proceeding to his home
was stopped by the Japanese Marines for the purpose of searching which
he refused the Marine then bayoneted him three times, he then crossed
over the creek into the Settlement, he was removed by the Fire Brigade
Ambulance to the Paulun Hospital. Dr.'s chit as follows:-

" Bayonet wound of left chest.
  Bayonet wound of left buttock.
  Bayonet wound of left palm."    Detained.

April 6, 1932.

Report on State of District Between 8 a.m.
5.4.32 and 8 a.m. 6.4.32.
--------------------------
Demonstrations arranged by
Students & Mill Workers.

The meetings arranged to take place at the following times and
places: 9 a.m. 11 a.m. and 2 p.m. at Robison and Ferry Roads corner,
South Tung Hwa Li off Robison Road and Macao Road. All passed off
quietly no meeting taking place owing to the precautions taken by the
Police and the Italian Marines. No.457 Penang Road, a Chinese house
at the East end of Nam Foo Lee on the North side of Penang Road was
visited by detectives from this station on instructions from the Spe-
cial Branch, the house is occupied by refugees and nothing further was
found.

Information has also been received from an informer to the effect
that ex-mill-workers will picket all rice shops for the purpose of
stealing rice on the 12.4.32.

Translation of posters found in Pootoo Road District as follows:
(批：Only one poster was seen - attached hereto)
EMERGENCY NOTICE
(批：抄) Since the Social Affairs Bureau (社會局), Local Peace Main-
tenance Association (地方維持會), Flood Relief Society (水災救
濟會) and other running dogs have formed an unemployed workers re-
lief they are leading us to our death. Here are the 3 plans they have
suggested:-

1) They order us to work in the Chinese Mills and have arranged with
the Capitalists to pay us 20 cents per day. Further all old wor-
kers will be dismissed.

2) There has been a big flood in our country and thousands upon thou-
sands are starving and they want to send us back home. That means
they also want us to die.

3) They are also trying to make us prisoners and take away our liberty
by sending us to refugee camps.

They want us to register and afterwards they will send our names
back to the Japanese. They will also ask the Police to arrest us.

关于1932年4月5日上午8时至1932年4月6日上午8时期间辖区状况的报告。
--------------------------
由学生及纱厂工人组织的示威活动。

原定于以下时间和地点举行的集会：上午9时、11时及下午2时，在罗宾森路与斐伦路转角、罗宾森路南面的东华里以及澳门路。由于警方及意大利海军陆战队采取了预防措施，所有集会均未举行，现场平静无事。根据特务科的指示，本巡捕房的侦探探访了槟榔路457号，这是一栋位于槟榔路北侧南福里东端的中式房屋，该房屋由难民居住，未发现其他情况。

另从线人处获悉，前纱厂工人将于1932年4月12日包围所有米店，目的是窃取大米。

在普陀路分区发现的标语翻译如下：
(批注：仅见到一张标语——附后)
紧急通告
(批注：抄录) 自从社会局、地方维持会、水灾救济会等走狗成立了失业工人救济机构以来，他们正引导我们走向死亡。以下是他们提出的三个方案：-

1) 他们命令我们去华资纱厂工作，并已与资本家安排每天支付我们20分钱。此外，所有老工人都将被解雇。

2) 我国发生了大水灾，成千上万的人正在挨饿，他们想把我们送回家乡。这意味着他们也想让我们死。

3) 他们还试图通过将我们送往难民营来使我们成为囚犯，剥夺我们的自由。

他们想让我们登记，然后将我们的名单送回给日本人。他们还会要求警察逮捕我们。

pages.en:
(2)

They also try to prohibit our Anti-Japanese activities in order to
collaborate with the Japanese Capitalists in oppressing our poor
workers.

Dear labour friends! Please do not go there to register your
names. Let us join up in our thousands and overwhelm them. Ask
them to give us rice and we can divide it ourselves. If you do this
we can defeat the Japanese Capitalists and all others with ease.

经查实，“卐字会”（Swastika Society）在槟榔路（Penang X Road，原文不清，疑为槟榔路或类似发音道路）O.O.L.的一处新建房屋群中为难民开设了一个收容所，难民来自嘉定、王渡（Wangdo，音译）、南翔和江湾。由一名叫冯松庭（Feng Soong Ting，音译）的人负责管理该收容所。目前人数为916人。

上海难民救济协会（X Shanghai Refugee Relief Society，原文前有X，可能指代不明或删改）也在罗宾森路（Robison Road）与胶州路（Kiaochow Road）交界处的O.O.L.，利用一些新建房屋和一家中国戏院，为来自利沃（Liwo，音译）、嘉定和宝山的1050名难民开设了一个收容所。由一名叫杨庆三（Yang Ching San，音译）的人负责管理该收容所。

175名难民进入租界，166名难民经由宜昌路桥离开。

      1,905人 居住在空置房屋内。

      5,020人

拘留16名华人。

华资纱厂情况，1932年3月28日上午无变化（原文误作so change，应为no change）。

特别科主管警官。

March 21, 1932.

Report on State of District Between 8 a.m.
20.3.32 and 8 a.m. 21.3.32.
------------------------------------

Shells found in District.

1. At 11.15 a.m. 20.3.32 C.P.C.3300 brought to the station one
unexploded shell which had been dug up by a farmer at the corner
of Seymour and Robison Roads.
2. At 3 p.m. C.P.C.3130 brought to station one unexploded shell
which had been dug up on Penang Road, near Gordon Road.

Shells will be handed over to Hongkew Station this A.M.

Request of Assistance by Japanese Mill O.O.L.
(See daily report dated 12.2.32).

Mr. Nishyima, Manager of the Kiwa Cotton Mill (Japan-China),
came to the station and requested assistance to remove a number of
workers from their quarters off Robison Road O.O.L. Enquiries by
the undersigned it was ascertained that there were still 500 mill
workers living in the quarters for which they paid no rent to the
management, the manager requested the Police to remove 9 persons
from the quarters as they were the cause of lot of trouble between
Japanese employees and the other Chinese ex-workers, the quarters
being in Chinese Territory assistance was asked of the Chinese
Police, 6th Division Robison Road Sub Station. Inspector Jefferson,
the undersigned and Sub Inspector Koo of the 6th Division proceeded
to the quarters, where it was agreed that the 9 persons concerned
should be removed. Sub Inspector Koo warned all concerned personal-
ly to remove by the 23rd, failing which further action would be taken
the manager stating that the remainder might stay on for the pre-
sent.

区内发现炮弹。

1. 1932年3月20日上午11时15分，警员C.P.C.3300将一枚未爆炸弹送至巡捕房，该炮弹由一名农夫在西摩路（Seymour Road）与罗宾森路（Robison Road）转角处挖出。
2. 下午3时，警员C.P.C.3130将一枚未爆炸弹送至巡捕房，该炮弹在槟榔路靠近戈登路处被挖出。

炮弹将于今晨移交虹口巡捕房。

日资纱厂外籍职员宿舍（O.O.L.）请求协助
（参见1932年2月12日的日报）。

日华纱厂经理西岛（Nishyima，音译）先生来到巡捕房，请求协助将数名工人从罗宾森路附近的外籍职员宿舍（O.O.L.）迁出。经本人查询，查明仍有500名纱厂工人居住在该宿舍内，且未向管理层支付租金。经理请求警方将9人从宿舍迁出，因为他们在日籍员工与其他前华人工人之间引起了许多麻烦。由于该宿舍位于中国领土内，故向中国警方求助，即第六分区罗宾森路分巡捕房。杰斐逊（Jefferson）督察、本人及第六分区的古（Koo，音译）副督察前往该宿舍，商定应将涉及的9人迁出。古副督察亲自警告所有相关人员须在23日前搬离，否则将采取进一步行动。经理表示其余人员目前可暂时留居。

Still far less than the volume of normally entering the
Settlement prior to the retreat of the Chinese Army.

Normal.

Further enquiries in Zau Ka Doo Village fail to reveal any
confirmation of the presence of strangers who could be suspected
of being plain clothes gunmen.

Curfew
Combined action of the Uniform and Crime Branches resulted
in the detention of 86 Chinese for breach of Curfew Regulations.
Released at 4a.m. 12-3-32.

                                            Chinese      2049

Shots fired during Curfew Hours
At about 11.30p.m. 11-3-32 Special Constable 210 Elm, halt-
ed a motorcar, Lic. No. 5550 being driven by Mr. C. Dettman, Ger.
of 26/24 Route Paul Henry, at Bubblingwell and Carter Roads corner.
The driver was ordered to proceed to B'well Station by S/C 210
who mounted the running board. They proceeded along Avenue Road,
around B'well Station and without stopping accelerated speed driv-
ing along B'well Road to Hardoon Road, where S/C 210 was thrown off
the running board. He thereupon fired 7 shots at the retreating
motorcar, which stopped and was taken to B'well Station by another
party which had been attracted by the sound of shots being fired.

宵禁期间发生的枪击事件
1932年3月11日晚约11时30分，特别巡捕210号埃尔姆（Elm，音译）在静安寺路与卡德路路口拦下一辆由亨利·保罗路26/24号居民、德国人C. Dettman先生驾驶的牌照号为5550的汽车。特别巡捕210号登上汽车踏板，命令司机驶往静安寺捕房。他们沿爱文义路行驶，绕过静安寺捕房，未作停留便加速沿静安寺路驶向哈同路，在此处特别巡捕210号从踏板上被甩下。他随即向正在逃离的汽车开了7枪，该车随后停下，并被另一批被枪声吸引而来的人带往静安寺捕房。

Reported Shooting at Armoured Car.

Road near Kiaochow Road. Lt. Bolders then hung up, and no further

turned out but the officer i/c Armoured Car explained that a shot

----------------------------------------

Unemployed Mill Workers Solici-
ting for Contributions.

At 10.30 a.m. 22.2.32 two groups of Chinese consisting of
1 Male and 2 females in each previously employed at the Kiwa
Mill were arrested in this district in possession of collecting
boxes and books, they were brought to the station cautioned and
released. They had no money in the boxes. Boxes and books re-
tained at the station.

Kiwa Mill Workers Registered with Social Bureau.

Between 1 p.m. and 3 p.m. 22.2.32 about 400 of the Kiwa
Mill workers attended at No.4615 Robison Road, an office opened
by the above workers, there were also present 3 members of the
Bureau of Social Affairs, these members were taking the names of
all the workers for the purpose of issuing the workers with rice,
during this time about 20 loafers attacked the three members of
the Bureau of Social Affairs stating that they wished to form
their own Committee, in the attack one of the members received
a slight cut on the head, the registering of names will carry on
until the 26.2.32 when the rice will be issued. Detectives have
been posted in the vicinity while the office is open to prevent
further trouble.

At 1.40 p.m. 21.2.32 J.P.S. 47 went to the Poo Ming
Hospital, Pootoo Road, to call a Doctor and was disarmed by
Pte. Minfrock U.S.M.C., who stated that he had orders to allow
no one to enter the Hospital armed. The Adjutant was inter-
viewed by Inspt. 1/S Holt who stated that it was due to a mis-
understanding and that he would issue orders to prevent possi-
ble recurrence.

14名男性和3名女性，系东兴纱厂及长棉会社第5和第8厂目前的失业工人，于1932年2月21日因持有募捐箱、横幅和收据簿而被捕。他们称是受青年会礼拜堂（罗宾森路荣华里后方）指示，代表失业纱厂工人进行募捐。箱子等物被扣留，被告获释。
日本警察署第47号被美国海军陆战队解除武装。
1932年2月21日下午1时40分，日本警察署第47号前往普陀路的普明医院请医生，被美国海军陆战队士兵明弗罗克（Minfrock）下士解除武装，该士兵称其奉命禁止任何人携带武器进入医院。霍尔特（Holt）一等巡官会见了副官，副官称这是由于误会，并将发布命令以防止类似情况再次发生。

47名日本妇女和儿童于1932年2月20日从戈登路181号东兴纱厂宿舍撤至杨树浦东兴纱厂宿舍。
医院。
1932年2月21日，20名男性和15名女性因在礼拜堂遭受枪伤而被送入巴利路48/9号的拉胡赛医院（Lahousaye' Hospital）。在拉胡赛医院和圣坛寺临时医院（Holy Tab Ts Temple）遭受枪伤的人数分别为79人和61人。总计135人。迄今收治总数169人，其中4人为儿童。

in the Foo Yih No.2 Cotton Mill, 8 Robison Road, four male
employees being injured names as follows:
1. Yan Vung Zai ( 邢 又 才 ).
2. Tsang Han Sze( 湯 漢 池 ).
3. Cheung San Foo ( 章 少 夫 ).
4. Dan Ying Kuo ( 閆 英 國 ).
taken to the Paulun Hospital by Shanghai Fire Brigade Ambulance.
Dr. certificates will be obtained to-day.

Yih Cotton Mill, 16 Makanchow Road and exploded, no one in-
jured, walls of building badly damaged and all windows shatter-
ed.

Dah Flour Mill, 3 Haens Road and exploded, small damage to
roof, no one injured.

detained 79.

February 18, 1932.

Report on State of District Between 8 a.m.
17.2.32 and 8 a.m. 18.2.32.
------------------------------------

Shells Dropped in this District.

1. One shell was found in the Tung Yih Cotton Mill, 10 Mekan-
shan Road having fallen during the early hours of the 17.2.32,
but did not explode. Shell removed by Police.

2. Shells were also found at the following addresses, all of
which did not explode. All removed to station by Police:
4665 Robison Road. 3990 Robison Road. 3918 Robison Road.
123 Gordon Road. One found on West Soochow Road.
Iung Hwa Li, off Robison Road. Slight damage to houses at
3990 Robison Road and 123 Gordon, no injuries.

3. At 9.45 a.m. 17.2.32 an Anti Air Craft shell fell in the
boiler room of the Tung Yih Cotton Mill, 10 Mokanshan Road and
exploded, no damage to boiler room, a coolie named Zung Yuin
Sing, age 20, residing at Chapei, employed at the above mill
was injured in the right leg. He was removed to the Paulun
Hospital by the Fire Brigade Ambulance. Dr's chit as follows:
"Two small wounds on right leg, dressed and allowed to go home".

4. At 9.55 a.m. 17.2.32 an Anti Air Craft shell fell exploded
in the Feu Foong Flour Mill, Mokanshan Road, no damage and no
one injured.

Re report of 8.30 a.m. 16.2.32 from further enquiries made
it was ascertained that the shell did not explode, the junk was
recovered from the creek, but so far the missing child has not
been found.
------------------------------------

Between 7 a.m. and 1 p.m. 17.2.32 about 700 workers of
various Japanese Mills, called at the Y.M.C.A., Robison Road
for the purpose of receiving rice and money which they had
been promised by representatives of the Social Bureau on the
16.2.32 has no representatives arrived by 1 p.m. about 400 of
the workers left to proceed to the Social Bureau, Kintao, but
on reaching the French Concession, were not allowed to proceed

（左侧手写批注：Received 18/2/32）

1. 1932年2月17日凌晨，一枚炮弹落在麦根山路10号同益棉纺厂，但未爆炸。炮弹已由警方移除。

2. 在以下地址也发现了炮弹，均未爆炸。全部由警方移至捕房：
罗宾森路4665号。罗宾森路3990号。罗宾森路3918号。
戈登路123号。西苏州路上发现一枚。
罗宾森路旁的荣华里。
罗宾森路3990号和戈登路123号的房屋轻微受损，无人受伤。

3. 1932年2月17日上午9时45分，一枚高射炮弹落在麦根山路10号同益棉纺厂的锅炉房并爆炸，锅炉房未受损，一名名叫Zung Yuin Sing（音译）、20岁、居住在闸北、受雇于上述工厂的苦力右腿受伤。由救火会救护车将其送往宝隆医院。医生诊断书如下：“右腿两处小伤口，已包扎，准予回家”。

4. 1932年2月17日上午9时55分，一枚高射炮弹落在麦根山路福丰面粉厂并爆炸，无损坏，无人受伤。

关于1932年2月16日上午8时30分的报告，经进一步查询获悉，该炮弹并未爆炸，舢板已从河中打捞上岸，但失踪儿童至今尚未找到。
------------------------------------

（左侧手写批注：1932年2月18日收悉）

pages.en:
"B"
Pestee Road Station.
February 17, 1932.
Report on State of District Between 8 a.m.
16.2.32 and 8 a.m. 17.2.32.
--------------------------
Mill Situation.
All Japanese Mills in this District remain closed this
A.M. 17.2.32.
The situation of Chinese Mills in this District, no
change this A.M. 17.2.32.
Re Opening of Mills.
The managers of the Zeng Sing Cotton Mill, Chapei,
Tung Yih Cotton Mill, 10 Mokanshan Road and Sung Sing Cotton
Mill, 2 Ichang Road, requested the Police to allow their
workers to leave the Settlement and vice and versa between
6 a.m. and 6 p.m. daily to attend work at the Mills. The
officer commanding these sectors were subsequently informed
permission has now been obtained from the Military for the
workers to resume work, providing that each worker be in
possession of a pay book and stamped by the Mills concerned
in Chinese and English.
Meeting held at the Y.M.C.A., Robison Road.
Between 10 a.m. and 12.10 p.m. on the 16.2.32 a meeting
of Mill workers about 200 attended at the Y.M.C.A., when five
representatives from the Society Bureau of Nantao attended,
names as follows:
Loh Nyi (毅), Siau Yih Kwei (蕭叶恢),
Chu Zung Yin (邱成蔭), Tien Cheng Pung (田正本)
and Lee Yan (李萬).
Then it was decided that all unemployed workers of the
various mills register their names. The representatives pro-
mised to obtain a quantity of rice and money for the workers
which would be given to the workers in due course.
pages.zh:

1932年2月17日。
关于1932年2月16日上午8时至1932年2月17日上午8时本区状况的报告。
--------------------------
纱厂情况。
本区内所有日资纱厂在1932年2月17日上午仍关闭。
本区内华资纱厂的情况，1932年2月17日上午无变化。
关于纱厂复工。
闸北增盛棉纺厂、莫干山路10号同义棉纺厂以及宜昌路2号松盛棉纺厂的经理请求警方允许其工人每日上午6时至下午6时进出租界前往纱厂上班。随后已通知负责这些区域的警官，军方现已准许工人复工，条件是每名工人须持有由相关纱厂用中英文盖章的工资簿。
在罗便臣路青年会举行的会议。
1932年2月16日上午10时至中午12时10分，约200名纱厂工人在青年会开会，南市社会局派出了五名代表出席，名单如下：
陆毅 (Loh Nyi)、萧叶恢 (Siau Yih Kwei)、
邱成蔭 (Chu Zung Yin)、田正本 (Tien Cheng Pung)
和李萬 (Lee Yan)。
会上决定，各纱厂所有失业工人均须登记姓名。代表们承诺为工人筹集一批大米和资金，并将在适当时候发放给工人。

pages.en:
(2)

Shells dropped in this District.

1. At 1.35 p.m. 16.2.32 one shell dropped in the Fou Feong
Flour Mill, and exploded damaging the wall of godown and a num-
ber of bags of flour. Two also dropped in the Soochow Creek,
no one injured.

2. At 4.10 a.m. 17.2.32 one shell exploded in No.1364 Robison
Road. Extensive damage to three rooms. Three persons injured:-
One male Loh Ser Shing ( 陸守興 ), one male Chian Ts Lien
( 蔣志連 ) and one female Van Lee Sz ( 范李氏 ).
Loh Ser Shing sent to Lester Chinese Hospital, the other two
sent to Paulum Hospital. Extent of injuries not yet ascertained.

3. At 4.25 a.m. 17.2.32 one shell entered 1349 Robison Road,
did not explode, no one injured. Damage to walls.

4. At 4.30 a.m. 17.2.32 one shell fell on roof of unnumbered
house in Tse Ah Fung (Peotoo Road) did not explode, no one in-
jured.

5. At about 3.30 a.m. 17.2.32 one shell exploded on a piece
of waste ground, Robison Road, slight damage to surrounding
shops, no one injured.

6. About 4.30 a.m. 17.2.32 a shell fell on temple, Gordon
Road, unexploded. No one injured. Slight damage to wall.

7. Three other unexploded shells were found in the vicinity
of Robison and Gordon Roads, which fell during the night.

8. About 4.30 a.m. 17.2.32 a shell exploded on a junk tied
up on Soochow Creek north of Penang Road Jetty. The Junk was
sunk, one child drowned and not recovered, one female seriously
wounded and one male Chinese dead (apparently from shock). Fe-
male sent to St. Elizabeth's Hospital by Fire Brigade Ambulance.

Remarks.

From enquiries made at the Labourers' Hospital, it was
ascertained that 30 persons admitted on the 16.2.32. Total
118.
pages.zh:
(2)

本区落下的炮弹。

1. 1932年2月16日下午1时35分，一枚炮弹落在福丰面粉厂内并爆炸，损坏了仓库墙壁及数袋面粉。另有两枚落入苏州河，无人受伤。

2. 1932年2月17日凌晨4时10分，一枚炮弹在罗便臣路1364号爆炸。三间房间严重受损。三人受伤：一名男子陆守兴 (Loh Ser Shing)，一名男子蒋志连 (Chian Ts Lien) 和一名女子范李氏 (Van Lee Sz)。
陆守兴被送往莱斯中国医院 (Lester Chinese Hospital)，另外两人被送往宝隆医院 (Paulum Hospital)。伤情程度尚未确定。

3. 1932年2月17日凌晨4时25分，一枚炮弹进入罗便臣路1349号，未爆炸，无人受伤。墙壁受损。

4. 1932年2月17日凌晨4时30分，一枚炮弹落在兆丰路（即北苏州路）一处无门牌房屋的屋顶上，未爆炸，无人受伤。

5. 1932年2月17日凌晨约3时30分，一枚炮弹在罗便臣路的一块空地上爆炸，周围店铺轻微受损，无人受伤。

6. 1932年2月17日凌晨约4时30分，一枚炮弹落在戈登路的一座庙宇上，未爆炸。无人受伤。墙壁轻微受损。

7. 在罗便臣路和戈登路附近发现了另外三枚夜间落下的未爆炮弹。

8. 1932年2月17日凌晨约4时30分，一枚炮弹在槟榔路码头以北的苏州河上一艘系泊的舢板上爆炸。舢板沉没，一名儿童溺水身亡且尸体未找到，一名女子重伤，一名中国男子死亡（显然死于惊吓）。该女子由消防队救护车送往圣伊丽莎白医院。

备注。

经向劳工医院查询，获悉1932年2月16日入院者30人。总计118人。

Shells Dropped in this District.
1. At about 9.45 p.m. 14.2.32, one shell dropped in the Fou
Foong Flour Mill, 25 Mokanshan Road, and did not explode, dama-
ge to brick wall, no one injured. Shell removed by U.S.Marines.
2. One also struck a Chinese house No.619 Mokanshan Road, but
did not explode, damage to roof and wall of house, afterwards
striking the wall of the Tung Yih Cotton Mill, 10 Mokanshan
Road, this also being damaged, no one injured.
3. One also struck a Godown in the Tung Yih Cotton Mill, 10
Mokanshan Road, damage to wall and godown, the shell was not
located, but a search will be made this A.M.
4. At 10 p.m. 14.2.32, two shells fell into two empty godowns
in the Fou Foong Flour Mill, 25 Mokanshan Road, but did not ex-
plode, shells removed by U.S. Marines and placed in the Soochow
Creek, damage at present unknown.

Mill Situation.
All Japanese Mills in this District remain closed this
A.M. 15.2.32.
The situation of the Chinese Mills, no change this A.M.
15.2.32.

Wounded.
Enquiries show that no wounded had been admitted to the
Labourers' Hospital between 8 a.m. 14.2.32 and 8 a.m. 15.2.32.

New Arrivals.
From enquiries made it was ascertained that there were no
new arrivals in this District.

Refugees.
About 200 refugees left this District by way of Ichang
Road Bridge, but no refugees entered.

February 14, 1932.

Report on State of District Between 8 a.m.
13.2.32 and 8 a.m. 14.2.32.
--------------------------

Shells Dropped in this District.

1. At 8.15 a.m. 13.2.32, a shell dropped on Mokanshan Road
outside of the Foh Sing Flour Mill and exploded. En-
quiries show that no damage was done and no persons in-
jured.

2. About 12 noon 13.2.32, a shell dropped at the corner of
Robison and Tonquin Roads, but did not explode. Shell
removed by U. S. Marines.

3. At 12.25 13.2.32, a shell fell on the roof of Price's
Candle Factory, 3 Robisen Road and exploded, damage to
roof and wall, no one injured.

4. See next page
Re Daily Report of the 12.2.32.

Japanese request for assistance to remove employees from
Mill Quarters Robisen Road, the following was received from
the Chinese Y. M. C. A. The manager was interviewed by
C.D.I. Robertson and D.S.I. Taplin on the 13.2.32, when he
stated he would allow the employees to remain pending a re-
ply to his application to the Shanghai Defence Force for pro-
tection of the Mill Property:

February 13th, 1932.

"Dear Sirs,

A few days ago, the Kiwa Mill posted a notice to the
effect, that all the workers, who live at the above mill
quarters, should remove before the 15th, inst.

As we found that it would be difficult for the workers
to find suitable houses, we therefore sent a representative
to interview Mr. Funatsu, the Chairman of the Japanese Mill
Association, who consented to have the workers remain in the
quarters, but we hope that you will give them protection and
obliges."

Y.M.C.A.
Robisen Road.

2. 1932年2月13日中午12时左右，一枚炮弹落在罗便臣路与汤肯路转角处，但未爆炸。炮弹由美国海军陆战队移除。

3. 1932年2月13日12时25分，一枚炮弹落在罗便臣路3号普赖斯蜡烛厂屋顶并爆炸，屋顶和墙壁受损，无人受伤。

4. 见下一页
关于1932年2月12日的日报。

日本人请求协助将其员工从罗便臣路的纱厂宿舍撤出，收到来自中华青年会的以下信函。1932年2月13日，罗伯逊首席侦探督察和塔普林副首席侦探督察会见了经理，经理表示，在他向上海防卫军申请保护纱厂财产的答复出来之前，他将允许员工留驻：

1932年2月13日。

“敬启者：

数日前，绮瓦纱厂张贴告示，大意是所有居住在上述纱厂宿舍的工人须在本月15日前搬离。

鉴于我们发现工人难以找到合适的住房，因此我们派代表会见了日本纱厂协会主席船津先生，他同意让工人留在宿舍内，但我们希望你们能给予他们保护，不胜感激。”

青年会
罗便臣路。

纱厂情况。

Report on State of District Between 8 a.m.
11.2.32 and 8 a.m. 12.2.32.
--------------------------

Mill Situation.

All Japanese Mills in this District remain closed
this A.M. 12.2.32.

The Situation of Chinese Mills: The workers re-
ported for duty A.M. 12.2.32 at the Sung Sing No.2 Mill,
Sing Dah Flour Mill and Pou Feeng Flour Mill, but did not
start work on account of the bomb which was dropped in Gor-
don Road District on the 11.2.32. It is not expected that
they will start work to-day.

Between 9.30 a.m. and 3.30 p.m. 11.2.32, 1595 Kiwa
Cotton Mills workers called at the Chinese Y.M.C.A., Robison
Road, and 2 pints of rice were given to each of the workers.

Japanese Request Protection O.C.L.

At 2.30 p.m. D.I. Shannon and D.S.I. Taplin inter-
viewed Mr. Nishikima of the Kiwa Mill, Robison Road, O.C.L.
who had requested assistance to protect the Mill property.
About 1500 workers are still living in the Mill quarters. A
notice has been posted for them to evacuate by the 13.2.32,
and the management are afraid of arson and damage to Mill
property. D.O."J" advised that the manager apply through
the Japanese Consul for adequate protection by Defence Force,
this being O.C.L. Two C.D.C's have been detailed for duty
in this vicinity to watch for Communists etc.

Wounded in Labourers' Hospital.

From enquiries made it was ascertained that 54 ad-
mitted on the 10.2.32 are still detained. 10 women wounded
in the Wing On Mill bomb explosion entered this Hospital at
12 noon 11.2.32.

New Arrivals.

Enquiries show there were about 20 new arrivals in
this District.

本区内所有日资纱厂在1932年2月12日上午仍关闭。

华资纱厂情况：松盛二厂、信大面粉厂和福丰面粉厂的工人于1932年2月12日上午报到，但由于1932年2月11日戈登路区投下炸弹，并未开始工作。预计他们今天不会开工。

1932年2月11日上午9时30分至下午3时30分之间，1595名绮瓦棉纺厂工人前往罗便臣路中华青年会，每位工人获发2品脱大米。

日本人请求当地指挥官提供保护。

下午2时30分，香农侦探督察和塔普林副首席侦探督察会见了罗便臣路绮瓦纱厂的西岛先生，他是当地指挥官，曾请求协助保护纱厂财产。约1500名工人仍居住在纱厂宿舍内。已张贴通知要求他们在1932年2月13日前撤离，管理层担心会发生纵火及纱厂财产受损。“J”区警官建议经理通过日本领事馆向防卫军申请充分保护，因为这是当地指挥官的职责。已派遣两名反共侦探在此附近执勤，监视共产党分子等。

<u>No Posters found in Western District.</u>

Enquiries were made at 31 Shien Chung Li, Robison
Road and No.6 Lane No.3 Yang Zung Terrace, Robison Road,
where it was ascertained that these offices had been opened
for the purpose of all the N.W.K. Mill employees to register
with a view to granting them an allowance of rice during
the present crisis.

<u>Report of Chinese Male Accidently
Shot by Italian Marine.</u>

At 4.05 p.m. a telephone message was received from
C.P.C.303 attached to Gordon Road Station that a Male Chinese
had been shot outside of the Kiu Mill, O.C.L. From En-
quiries made by D.I. Sharman and the undersigned it was as-
certained, that a Male Chinese named Zoo Ah Hyi (徐阿二),
age 39 years, native of Kunpo, hawker, residing on the north
bank of the Soochow Creek, Chapei. At 3.50 p.m. he was pro-
ceeding along the side of the Creek when he was struck by a
bullet fired by an Italian Marine, he was removed to the
St. Luke's Hospital by an American Marines' M/truck, where
he is at present detained. Dr's chit as follows:

"Gun shot wound of chest. May become serious".

Further enquiries at the Italian Marine Post it was
ascertained that the shot had been fired by a Marine named
Tarantino accidently, this Marine was on guard at the time,
his rifle being rested on the sand-bags loaded,when he went
to remove same he accidently touched the trigger.

<u>Wounded.</u>

From enquiries made it was ascertained that 21 Male
and 25 Female were removed from a Hospital in Chapei to the
Labourers' Hospital at 46 Ferry Road, these persons having
been previously wounded during the fighting in Chapei.

（批：Recorded）

<u>西区未发现张贴海报。</u>

经向罗宾森路贤忠里31号及罗宾森路杨宗台3弄6号查询，获悉这些办事处已开放，供西北纱厂所有员工登记，以便在当前危机期间向他们发放米贴。

<u>中国男子被意大利海军陆战队员意外枪击的报告。</u>

下午4时05分，戈登路捕房附属的第303号中央电话交换台打来电话称，一名中国男子在O.C.L.（原文不清，可能指某地点或公司缩写）的久丰纱厂外被枪击。经分区督察长夏曼（Sharman）及具名者查询，查明受害者名为徐阿二（Zoo Ah Hyi），39岁，江苏昆山人，小贩，居住在闸北苏州河北岸。下午3时50分，他沿河边行走时，被一名意大利海军陆战队员发射的子弹击中。他被美国海军陆战队的一辆摩托卡车送往圣卢克医院，目前留院治疗。医生诊断书如下：

“胸部枪伤。可能恶化”。

经进一步向意大利海军陆战队哨所查询，查明开枪者为一名名叫塔兰蒂诺（Tarantino）的海军陆战队员，系意外走火。当时该士兵正在站岗，步枪架在装满的沙袋上，他在移动步枪时意外触动了扳机。

<u>伤者。</u>

经查询查明，21名男性和25名女性从闸北的一家医院被转移至渡船路46号的劳工医院，这些人在此前闸北的战斗中受伤。

Pestee Road Station.
February 7, 1932.

Report on State of District Between 8 a.m.
6.2.32 and 8 a.m. 7.2.32.

Shells Dropped in this District.

1. At about 9.20 a.m. 6.2.32, a number of shells were dropped
in this district, 4 of these dropped and exploded on Ton-
quin Road, between Haase and Pestee Road, no persons were
injured.

（批：Received）

2. One dropped on a Chinese House situated No.138 Tonquin
Road and exploded, causing slight damage to the roof, and
slight injuring to one named Weng Tsung Sai (王春山)
who was in the house at the time. He was sent to the Pau-
lum Hospital and for dressing. Dr's chit as follows:
"Bomb wound in right arm. Not serious".

3. One dropped at the rear of the N.W.K. Mill, 62 Robison
Road and exploded, wounding one named Tsang Zang Ngau
(張長敖), a coolie, employed at the above mill. He
was removed to the Paulum Hospital by the Fire Brigade Am-
bulance. Dr's chit as follows:
"Bomb wound in buttock. Not serious, not detained".

4. One fell in a Chinese House at 797 Pestee Road and exploded
but slight damage to roof, chairs and tables.

5. One fell in a Chinese House at 163 Tonquin Road and ex-
ploded, also doing slight damage to roof, no one injured.

Mill Situation.

All Japanese and Chinese owned Mills in this District
remain closed this A.M. 7.2.32.

New Arrivals.

As far as can be ascertained there were 40 new arrivals
in this District.

1932年2月7日。

关于1932年2月6日上午8时至1932年2月7日上午8时本区状况的报告。

本区落弹情况。

1. 1932年2月6日上午9时20分左右，多枚炮弹落入本区，其中4枚落在哈斯路与培斯塔路之间的通肯路上并爆炸，无人受伤。

（批注：已收到）

2. 一枚落在通肯路138号的一所华宅内并爆炸，造成屋顶轻微损坏，并致当时在屋内的王春山（Weng Tsung Sai）轻伤。他被送往宝隆医院包扎。医生诊断书如下：
“右臂炸弹伤。不严重”。

3. 一枚落在罗宾森路62号西北纱厂后方并爆炸，致在该厂做工的苦力张长敖（Tsang Zang Ngau）受伤。他被消防队救护车送往宝隆医院。医生诊断书如下：
“臀部炸弹伤。不严重，未留院”。

4. 一枚落在培斯塔路797号的一所华宅内并爆炸，仅对屋顶、桌椅造成轻微损坏。

5. 一枚落在通肯路163号的一所华宅内并爆炸，亦对屋顶造成轻微损坏，无人受伤。

工厂情况。

1932年2月7日上午，本区内所有日资和华资工厂均处于关闭状态。

新抵人员。

据查，本区有40名新抵人员。

7 Chinese.

February 6, 1932.

Report on State of District Between 8 a.m.
5.2.32 and 8 a.m. 6.2.32.
----------------------------------------
Report of Japanese Mills guarded by
British and American Forces.

Re daily report of the 4.2.32, when the British forces
took over the N.W.K. Mills from the Japanese Marines, N.W.K.
No.1 & 2 Mills, 62 Robison Road O.O.L. and Japanese Quarters
on Penang Road. It has since been ascertained that the follow-
ing Mills were taken over by the American Marines on the 4.2.32.

N.W.K. Nos. 3 & 4 Mills, 19 West Soochow Road.
Japanese Quarters, 17 Ichang Road.
N.W.K. Nos. 5, 6 & 7 Mills, 14 West Soochow Road.
N.W.K. Mill Quarters, Haase Road.
N.W.K. No.8 Mill, 146 Gordon Road.
Dong Shing Cotton Mill, 151 Gordon Road.
Japanese Hospital, 161 Haase Road.
----------------------------------------
Report on shells dropped in
Pootoo Road District.

1. At about 11 a.m. 5.2.32, a number of shells were dropped
in this district. Enquiries were made and it was ascer-
tained that one shell had exploded at Price's Candle Factory,
No.5 Robison Road, damage to roof of godown, there were no
persons injured.

2. Tung Yih Cotton Mill, 10 Moulmein Road, one shell dropped
in the cotton mill but did not explode, damage to wall and 12
panes of glass broken.

3. One fell on a piece of vacant land at the corner of Gordon
and Moulmein Roads, but did not explode.

4. One fell in a Chinese House next door from No 14 Albany
off Moulmein Road. Exploded, slight damage to roof, none
injured.

5. One fell in the garden of No7 Moulmein Road, exploding, no
damage and no one injured.

1932年2月6日。

关于1932年2月5日上午8时至1932年2月6日上午8时本区状况的报告。
----------------------------------------
由英美军队守卫的日本纱厂报告。

根据1932年2月4日的日报，当英军从日本海军陆战队手中接管西北纺织株式会社（N.W.K.）纱厂时，涉及位于罗宾森路62号的西北纺织第一、二纱厂及老闸捕房辖区（O.O.L.），以及槟榔路上的日本宿舍。此后查明，以下纱厂已于1932年2月4日由美国海军陆战队接管：

西北纺织第三、四纱厂，西苏州路19号。
日本宿舍，宜昌路17号。
西北纺织第五、六、七纱厂，西苏州路14号。
西北纺织纱厂宿舍，赫司克路（Haase Road）。
西北纺织第八纱厂，戈登路146号。
东兴棉纺厂，戈登路151号。
日本医院，赫司克路161号。
----------------------------------------
关于普陀路区内落下炮弹的报告。

1. 1932年2月5日上午11时许，数枚炮弹落入本区。经查询，查明一枚炮弹在罗宾森路5号普赖斯蜡烛厂爆炸，造成仓库屋顶受损，无人受伤。

2. 莫利蒙路10号通益棉纺厂，一枚炮弹落入棉纺厂内但未爆炸，墙体受损，12块玻璃破碎。

3. 一枚落在戈登路与莫利蒙路转角处的一块空地上，未爆炸。

4. 一枚落在莫利蒙路旁奥尔巴尼路14号隔壁的一户华人住宅内。爆炸，屋顶轻微受损，无人受伤。

5. 一枚落在莫利蒙路7号的花园内，爆炸，无损坏，无人受伤。

pages.en:
(2)

6. One Anti Air-craft (Pom Pom) shell struck a Butcher's
Meat block out-side of a shop on Ferry Road, near Robi-
son Road, no damage and no one injured.

7. One fell at the corner of Penang and Robison Roads and
exploded, two persons injured, one small girl injuring
to leg and face, taken away by Chapel Police, name un-
known. One male named Wong Tseong Hou (王志厚),
age 35, native of Honan, residing at 4 Robison Road,
injured in right leg, sent to Chinese Lester Hospital.
Dr's. chit as follows:
"Bomb wound of leg. Not serious."

8. One fell on McKenzie Road, about 100 yards east of
Tonquin Road and exploded injuring a Male Chinese,
named Wong Zang Sung (王長生), age 50, native of
Whaich, residing at No.2 Tonquin Road and employed as a
Private Watchman at the Foh Shing Flour Mill, he was
removed to the Paulum Hospital by the Fire Brigade Am-
bulance and detained. Dr's chit as follows:
"Bomb wound of right leg. Not serious".

All shells that did not explode were removed by the
Police and placed in the Soochow Creek.

Mills Situations.

All Japanese and Chinese owned Mills in this Dis-
trict remain closed this A.M. 6.2.38.

New Arrivals.

As far as can be ascertained there were no new
arrivals in this District.

Rumours.

Enquiries at Hongkew it was learned that no rumours
had been circulated in this District.
pages.zh:
(2)

6. 一枚防空（砰砰炮）炮弹击中斐伦路靠近罗宾森路一家店铺外的一块肉铺砧板，无损坏，无人受伤。

7. 一枚落在槟榔路与罗宾森路转角处并爆炸，两人受伤，一名小女孩腿部和面部受伤，由教堂巡捕带走，姓名不详。一名男子名为王志厚（Wong Tseong Hou），35岁，河南籍，居住于罗宾森路4号，右腿受伤，送往华人莱斯德医院（Lester Hospital）。医生诊断书如下：
“腿部炸弹伤。不严重。”

8. 一枚落在麦肯齐路，汤昆路以东约100码处并爆炸，致一名华籍男子受伤，名为王长生（Wong Zang Sung），50岁，怀庆籍，居住于汤昆路2号，受雇于福新面粉厂担任私人看守，由消防队救护车送至宝隆医院（Paulum Hospital）并留院观察。医生诊断书如下：
“右腿炸弹伤。不严重”。

所有未爆炸的炮弹均由警方移除并投入苏州河。

纱厂情况。

新抵人员。

据查，本区无新抵人员。

谣言。

pages.en:
"B" Division.
Pootoo Road Station.
February 3, 1932.

Report on State of District between 8 a.m. 2.2.32
and 8 a.m. 3.2.32.
------------------

Unrest of Workers at Price's Candle Factory.

At 5 p.m. on the 1.2.32 Mr. Marjesson, Manager of the above
factory at 5 Robison Road, came to the station and requested
Police assistance while he was dealing with certain demands made
by 125 coolies employed at the above factory. It appears that
for the past two years the management have given the workers a
Bonus of $6.00 with 5 days holidays and 2 days pay, this being
due to the fact that they were only working part time, and this
year the management decided to only give a Bonus of $4.00 as
the workers had been working full time. At 7 a.m. 2.2.32 a party
of Police attended the factory, but the workers had agreed to
the new conditions.
------------------

Mill Situation.

All Japanese and Chinese owned Mills in this District remain
closed this A.M.
------------------

Rice stolen from Rice Shop.

At about 12 noon 2.2.32 about 100 Chinese of the mill worker
class forced their way into a rice shop at 1451-2-3 Robison Road
and stole 100 bags of rice. Information was received at the
station and a large party of Police proceeded to the scene and
succeeded in taking 10 men into custody and recovered a part of
the stolen property.
------------------

Japanese and Chinese Remove from Settlement.

About 13 Japanese residing on Robison Road removed to the
N.V.K. Mill Quarters at Macao Road. I was also noticed that a
number of Japanese female and children were removed from the
Japanese Hospital on Pootoo Road.

I would also like to point out that Japanese Inspector
pages.zh:
"B"分区。
普陀路捕房。
1932年2月3日。

关于1932年2月2日上午8时至1932年2月3日上午8时本区状况的报告。
------------------

普赖斯蜡烛厂工人骚动。

1932年2月1日下午5时，上述工厂经理马杰森先生（Mr. Marjesson，地址罗宾森路5号）来到捕房，请求警方协助他处理该厂125名苦力提出的某些要求。据悉，过去两年管理层给予工人6美元奖金，附带5天假期和2天薪水，这是因为他们仅从事兼职工作；而今年管理层决定仅给予4美元奖金，因为工人们一直在从事全职工作。1932年2月2日上午7时，一队警察前往工厂，但工人们已同意新条件。
------------------

纱厂情况。

本区内所有日资和华资纱厂在今晨仍关闭。
------------------

米店大米被盗。

1932年2月2日中午12时许，约100名属于纱厂工人阶层的华人强行闯入罗宾森路1451-2-3号的一家米店，偷走100袋大米。捕房接到情报后，一大队警察赶赴现场，成功拘留10人并追回部分失窃财物。
------------------

日本人和华人撤离租界。

约13名居住在罗宾森路的日本人搬迁至澳门路的日清汽船株式会社（N.V.K.）纱厂宿舍。我还注意到，一些日本妇女和儿童从普陀路的日本医院撤离。

我还要指出，日本巡官

pages.en:
(2)
Shibuye, J.D.S. 1 and J.D.C. 88, attached to this Station, re-
moved their wifes and families to the Hongkew District.
It was also ascertained that a large number of Chinese
were removing from Robison Road. On enquiries being made it
was ascertained that the people were leaving owing to being
out of employment and that they were proceeding to the country.
-------------------------
Report of Plain Cloths Chinese Soldiers Entering
the Settlement.
At 5.30 p.m. a telephone message was received from the
In Charge of the No.6 Division Chapei Police, reporting that
about 500 Plain Clothes Soldiers had entered the Yah Sui Loong
Alleyway off Ferry Road from the north side of the Soochow
Creek and were proceeding towards Ferry Road. A party of Police
attended but failed to locate any of the men. A visit was made
to the Chapei Sub-Station, where it was ascertained that at
about 10 a.m. this inst. (2.2.32) a party of 6 Plain Clothes
men wearing yellow silk badges, called on the Sub-Station and
asked for an escort stating that they wished to proceed to the
Settlement unarmed, this was refused by the Chapei Police. It
was learned from the Chapei Police that about 300 of these Plain
Clothes men had entered the Settlement by crossing the Soochow
Creek, there appears to be a great deal of doubt in this informa-
tion has nothing was reported by the defence forces guarding
this section.
-------------------------
Refugees.
No refugees were reported to have entered the Settlement
during the 2.2.31. But it was noticed that about 800 persons
left the Settlement crossing over the Soochow Creek.
-------------------------
New Arrivals.
As far as can be ascertained there were no new arrivals in
this District.
-------------------------
Wounded.
No wounded have been admitted to Hospitals in this District.
pages.zh:
(2)
涩谷（Shibuye），J.D.S. 1 和 J.D.C. 88，隶属本捕房，将其妻子和家人迁往虹口区。
还查明，大量华人正从罗宾森路搬离。经查询，查明这些人离开是因为失业，他们正前往内地。
-------------------------
关于便衣华兵进入租界的报告。
下午5时30分，接到闸北捕房第六分区主管的电话留言，报告称约500名便衣士兵从苏州河北侧进入斐伦路旁的亚水龙弄（Yah Sui Loong Alleyway），并向斐伦路方向行进。一队警察前往查看，但未能找到任何人。随后访问了闸北分捕房，查明当日（1932年2月2日）上午10时许，一队6名佩戴黄色丝绸臂章的便衣人员拜访分捕房，要求护送，声称希望 unarmed（不带武器）前往租界，此举被闸北捕房拒绝。从闸北捕房获悉，约300名此类便衣人员已越过苏州河进入租界，但该消息似乎大有可疑，因为守卫该段的防御部队并未报告任何情况。
-------------------------
难民。
据报道，1932年2月2日期间无难民进入租界。但注意到约800人越过苏州河离开租界。
-------------------------

"Y" Division.
Posteo Road Station.
February 3, 1932.

Report on State of District between 8 a.m. 2.2.32
and 8 a.m. 3.2.32.
------------------

Unrest of Workers at Price's Candle Factory.

At 5 p.m. on the 1.2.32 Mr. Marjessen, Manager of the above
factory at 5 Robinson Road, came to the station and requested
Police assistance while he was dealing with certain demands made
by 125 coolies employed at the above factory. It appears that
for the past two years the management have given the workers a
Bonus of $6.00 with 5 days holidays and 2 days pay, this being
due to the fact that they were only working part time, and this
year the management decided to only give a Bonus of $4.00 has
the workers had been working full time. At 7 a.m. 2.2.32 a party
of Police attended the factory, but the workers had agreed to
the new conditions.

------------------

Mill Situation.

All Japanese and Chinese owned Mills in this District remain
closed this A.M.

------------------

Rice stolen from Rice Shop.

At about 12 noon 2.2.32 about 100 Chinese of the mill worker
class forced their way into a rice shop at 1451-2-3 Robinson Road
and stole 100 bags of rice. Information was received at the
station and a large party of Police proceeded to the scene and
succeeded in taking 10 men into custody and recovered a part of
the stolen property.

------------------

Japanese and Chinese remove from Settlement.

About 10 Japanese families in Robinson Road removed to the
Indian Mill Quarters at Pasir Road. I was also noticed that a
number of Japanese women and children were removed from the
Chinese quarters in China Town.
pages.zh:
"Y"分区。
Posteo路捕房。
1932年2月3日。

关于1932年2月2日上午8时至1932年2月3日上午8时本区状况的报告。
------------------

普赖斯蜡烛厂工人骚动。

1932年2月1日下午5时，上述工厂经理马杰森先生（Mr. Marjessen，地址罗宾森路5号）来到捕房，请求警方协助他处理该厂125名苦力提出的某些要求。据悉，过去两年管理层给予工人6美元奖金，附带5天假期和2天薪水，这是因为他们仅从事兼职工作；而今年管理层决定仅给予4美元奖金，因为工人们一直在从事全职工作。1932年2月2日上午7时，一队警察前往工厂，但工人们已同意新条件。

------------------

纱厂情况。

本区内所有日资和华资纱厂在今晨仍关闭。

------------------

米店大米被盗。

1932年2月2日中午12时许，约100名属于纱厂工人阶层的华人强行闯入罗宾森路1451-2-3号的一家米店，偷走100袋大米。捕房接到情报后，一大队警察赶赴现场，成功拘留10人并追回部分失窃财物。

------------------

日本人和华人撤离租界。

罗宾森路约10户日本家庭搬迁至帕西尔路（Pasir Road）的印资纱厂宿舍。我还注意到，一些日本妇女和儿童从中国城的华人居住区撤离。

pages.en:
(2)

Shibuye, J.D.S. 1 and J.D.C. 88, attached to this Station, re-
moved their wives and families to the Hongkew District.

It was also ascertained that a large number of Chinese
were removing from Robison Road. On enquiries being made it
was ascertained that the people were leaving owing to being
out of employment and that they were proceeding to the country.

Report of Plain Clothes Chinese Soldiers Entering
the Settlement.

At 5.30 p.m. a telephone message was received from the
In Charge of the No.4 Division Chapei Police, Reporting that
about 200 Plain Clothes Soldiers had entered the Yah Sui Leong
Alleyway off Ferry Road from the north side of the Soochow
Creek and were proceeding towards Ferry Road. A party of Police
attended but failed to locate any of the men. A visit was made
to the Chapei Sub-Station, where it was ascertained that at
about 10 a.m. this inst. (2.2.32) a party of 6 Plain Clothes
men wearing yellow silk badges, called on the Sub-Station and
asked for an escort stating that they wished to proceed to the
Settlement unarmed, this was refused by the Chapei Police. It
was learned from the Chapei Police that about 200 of these Plain
Clothes men had entered the Settlement by crossing the Soochow
Creek, there appears to be a great deal of doubt in this informa-
tion as nothing was reported by the defence forces guarding
this section.

Refugees.

No refugees were reported to have entered the Settlement
during the 2.2.32. But it was noticed that about 200 persons
left the Settlement crossing over the Soochow Creek.

New Arrivals.

As far as can be ascertained there were no new arrivals in
this District.

Deaths.

No unusual have been reported to Hospitals in this District.

涩谷（Shibuye），J.D.S. 1 和 J.D.C. 88，隶属本捕房，将其妻子和家人迁往虹口区。

还查明，大量华人正从罗宾森路搬离。经查询，查明这些人离开是因为失业，他们正前往内地。

关于便衣华兵进入租界的报告。

下午5时30分，接到闸北捕房第四分区主管的电话留言，报告称约200名便衣士兵从苏州河北侧进入斐伦路旁的亚水龙弄（Yah Sui Leong Alleyway），并向斐伦路方向行进。一队警察前往查看，但未能找到任何人。随后访问了闸北分捕房，查明当日（1932年2月2日）上午10时许，一队6名佩戴黄色丝绸臂章的便衣人员拜访分捕房，要求护送，声称希望 unarmed（不带武器）前往租界，此举被闸北捕房拒绝。从闸北捕房获悉，约200名此类便衣人员已越过苏州河进入租界，但该消息似乎大有可疑，因为守卫该段的防御部队并未报告任何情况。

难民。

据报道，1932年2月2日期间无难民进入租界。但注意到约200人越过苏州河离开租界。

新抵人员。

据查，本区无新抵人员。

死亡。

本区医院未报告异常死亡情况。

Sir,
At about 6 p.m. tonight a slip of paper was given to Inspector i/c Kee Yung Dam (顧文濤 ) of the No.6 Division Bureau of Public Safety Robinson Road Sub-Station by a Japanese in the Nos. 1 & 2 N.Y.K. Mills, Robinson Road, warning him not to stop a motor car the number of which is believed to be 3309. At 6.40 p.m. a lorry laden with about 10 Japanese Marines drew up outside of the above-mentioned mill and were about to enter when they were called upon by a Chapel Policeman on duty at the entrance to the sub-station, which is next door to the mill to give the pass-word. The Japanese immediately dismounted from the lorry and opened fire on the policeman who immediately withdrew into an adjacent alley-way. Between 40 and 50 shots were fired by the Japanese and none at all by the Chapel Police. As far as can be ascertained nobody was injured.

The above information was given by Chapel Police Constable No.1168 Zam Fah Zang (晁福盛 ).

A C.P.C. on duty on Robinson Road hearing shots telephoned the Station whereupon a party of Police and detectives attended, but remained at the Settlement gate on Robinson Road. S.I. Browning and the undersigned closed the Settlement gate and proceeded to the Sub-Station. A number of spent cartridges were found on the ground immediately in front of the Sub-Station, they were all of Japanese pattern and about .303 calibre. D.O."B" Division Major Wainwright who had been notified arrived on the scene about this time and whilst inspecting the Sub-Station a number (about 8) of Japanese Marines headed by a Japanese civilian formed up in front in the Station whilst several went inside. They afterwards came out escorting some Chapel Policemen, one of whom appeared to be

今晚约6时，罗宾森路第六分区公安局分署主管督察顾文濤（Kee Yung Dam）收到一张由罗宾森路内外棉株式会社第一和第二纱厂内的一名日本人递来的纸条，警告他不要拦截一辆车牌号疑似为3309的汽车。下午6时40分，一辆载有约10名日本海军陆战队士兵的卡车停在该纱厂外，正欲进入时，被在紧邻纱厂的分署入口处执勤的一名教堂巡捕要求出示口令。日本人立即从卡车上下来，向该巡捕开火，该巡捕随即撤入附近的一条弄堂。日本人开了约40至50枪，教堂巡捕未还击。据所能查明的情况，无人受伤。

以上信息由教堂巡捕第1168号晁福盛（Zam Fah Zang）提供。

一名在罗宾森路执勤的教堂巡捕听到枪声后致电捕房，随后一队警察和侦探赶到，但停留在罗宾森路的租界大门处。副督察长 Browning 和在下的封闭了租界大门，并前往分署。在分署正前方的地面上发现了许多空弹壳，均为日式规格，口径约为.303。此时，已获通知的 *B* 分区警司 Wainwright 少校抵达现场，在检查分署时，约8名由一名日本平民带领的日本海军陆战队士兵在分署前列队，另有几人进入内部。随后他们出来时护送着几名教堂巡捕，其中一人似乎是

D R.
1932年1月31日。

8 a.m. 30.1.32.

Made by D.S.I. Taplin. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
About 3 p.m. today bombs were dropped on the Dah Foong
Cotton Mill (Chinese) on the Chinese side of the Soochow Creek,
opposite the intersection of Tonquin and Hokanshan Roads. It is
believed that the mill was full of workers at the time of the
attack. A large number of workers jumped into the Soochow Creek,
but were turned back.
The bombs exploded but the extent of damage is not known
or if there was any loss of life.
------------------------------------
F.P.S. Cook reported that during the day with the assistance
of the American Marines about 10,000 refugees attempted to cross
the Soochow Creek, but were turned back.
------------------------------------
Detectives found posters purporting to emanate from the
Shanghai Special District Citizens' Union on Robison Road this
afternoon. Translation as follows :- "As the Japanese Army has
brutally invaded China, go on strike to protect the same ".
A copy is appended herewith.
------------------------------------

[Signature]
D.S.I.

D.C. (Crime).
[Signature] [Signature]

Subject (in full) Lock out in Silk Filatures situated in West Hongkew District.

Made by D.P.S. Wright. Forwarded by J B Cleaves Insp.

Sir.
At 8am 24/9/32 C.P.C. 635 reported by telephone to the station
that the employees of the Loong Yuen Silk Filature (隆元),
No 11 Alabaster Road, had ceased work at the instigation of the
management, due to a threat of intimidation from striking employees
of the silk filatures situated in Chapei. Detectives instigated
inquires as the result of which, the following particulars were
ascertained. A number of striking employees from silk filatures
situated in Chapei, gathered outside the above mentioned silk
filature, and threatened the employees to cease work. The manage-
ment of the concern in order to prevent an outbreak of trouble
ordered the employees to cease work. As the result of the afore-
mentioned decision on the part of this particular filature, the
management of the appended silk filatures also decided to instruct
their employees to cease work.

All the silk filatures are expected to resume work tomorrow.
Herewith appended a list of silk filatures and numbers of emp-
loyees employed in each filature, who are at present idle.

Ziang Fong (祥豐), 132 Kansuh Road, employees 400 females.
Z Ziang (绪祥), 11 Alabaster Road, employees 370 females.
Chien Wei (经緯), 47 Alabaster Road, employees 400 females.
Zung Chong (润昌), 47 Alabaster Road, employees 400 females.
Loong Yuen (隆元), 11 Alabaster Road, employees 250 females.

Police and detectives have been posted in the vicinity of the
filatures to prevent sabotage and intimidation.

Subject (in full) Alleged ultimatum delivered by Japanese Naval Forces to Chinese
Authorities for the evacuation of Chapei and Paoshan Areas.

Made by D.S.I. White. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
At about 5.15 p.m. the 2-9-32, Mr. Grey, Shanghai-Nanking Railway,
came to the station and requested confirmation in respect to certain
information he had received from employees of the Shanghai-Nanking
Railway regarding an ultimatum alleged to have been delivered to the
Chinese Authorities by the Japanese Naval Forces for the evacuation
of the Chinese officials.

D.S.I. Hill, C.D.B.I. Chu Chi Huang and Voong Pah Zung immediately
proceeded to the 5th Division Public Safety Bureau Headquarters,
Paoshan Road and interviewed Colonel Ho, who stated that no such
ultimatum had been received and that there was no foundation to the
rumour.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently.
R J White D.S.I.

Sen. Det.
（批：The 4th Div were also visited with Same Results.
From Enquiries it was ascertained that a number
D.D.O. "C" Div of Locomotives at the North Station on the
night of the 2nd were keeping up Steam; and
（左侧标注：Re Cris Branch） their % Immediate departure & Sort of
Reasons given, thus. This shows to
what Extent the Railway Staff are behind
the Rumour.
Q Y Aids ano）

West Hongkew Station,

Date June 13th 19 32

Subject (in full) Proceedings at Memorial Service for Chinese killed
during Sino-Japanese hostilities.

Made by D.S.I. Gash Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
At about 5.00 a.m. June 13, 50 uniform armed policemen
and 40 Chinese detectives of the Bureau of Public Safety arrived
in motor lorries at the Chinese General Chamber of Commerce,
North Honan Road. They were followed at 6.00 a.m. by 30
members of the National Salvation Army of the Shanghai Citizen's
Federation and 100 Boy Scouts and two military bands totalling
60 persons, one from the Garrison Headquarters and one from the
Bureau of Public Safety.

The memorial service commenced at 10.35 a.m. and lasted
until 11.20 a.m. during which period speeches were made by
following notables :-
General Tsai Ting Kai, Commanding the 19th Route Army; Wong
Chao Lai, Chairman of the Chamber of Commerce; Wong Ying Sing,
Chief of the Bureau of Public Safety.
Among those present were :- Mayor Wu Teh Chen,
Li Yun Ziang, Director of the meeting; Tsang Yih Sung, Vice
director of the meeting; Waung Kuung, Representing the Chapei
Police; Lieu Zoong Ying, Vice representative of the Chapei Poli
Dzung Zung Tsing, Chairman of the Reception Committee; Dzung
Koch Zung, Vice Chairman of the Reception Committee; Tsang Tu
Kyi, Chief of the National Salvation Army; Wong Ming, Deputy
Chief of the National Salvation Army; and Zaw Ts Kong and Sih
Kwong Zen who read the memorial service.

The service passed off without untoward incident and all
the guests together with the squad of Special Police from the
Bureau of Public Safety had left the premises by 12.00 noon.

[Signature]
D.D.O."C"
O.i/c Special Branch.

[Signature]
D. S. I.

追悼仪式于上午10时35分开始，持续至上午11时20分，期间以下知名人士发表了演讲：
第十九路军指挥官蔡廷锴将军；商会主席王肇莱（Wong Chao Lai）；公安局局长黄英生（Wong Ying Sing）。

会议总监李云江（Li Yun Ziang）；会议副总监曾义松（Tsang Yih Sung）；代表闸北警方的王光（Waung Kuung）；闸北警方副代表刘宗英（Lieu Zoong Ying）；接待委员会主席张宗庆（Dzung Zung Tsing）；接待委员会副主席张克忠（Dzung Koch Zung）；救国军总指挥张图基（Tsang Tu Kyi）；救国军副总指挥王明（Wong Ming）；以及宣读祭文的赵子公（Zaw Ts Kong）和施广珍（Sih Kwong Zen）。

File No............
West Hongkew Station,
REPORT
Date June 13th 1932

Subject (in full) Proceedings at Memorial Service for Chinese killed
during Sino-Japanese hostilities.

Made by D.S.I. (Spt) Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

At about 5.30 p.m. June 11, 30 uniformed policemen
and 10 plain clothes of the Bureau of Public Safety arrived
in motor lorries at the Chinese General Chamber of Commerce,
North Honan Road. They were followed at 6.00 p.m. by 30
members of the National Salvation Army of the Shanghai Citizen's
Federation and 100 boy scouts and two military bands totalling
60 persons, all from the Russian Band quarter to act as bearers from the
chamber of public safety.

The memorial service commenced at 10.30 a.m. and lasted
until 11.30 a.m. during which period speeches were made by
following notables :-

General T'ang Ting K'ai, Commanding the 19th Route Army; Sung
Jihao Lai, Chairman of the Chamber of Commerce; Heng Ying Sing,
Chief of the Bureau of Public Safety.

Among those present were :- Mayor Wu Teh Chen,

Li Yung Chiang, Director of the meeting; Tsang Yin Neng, Vice
director of the meeting; Tsang Kung, representing the Chapei
Police; Hieu Zoong Yiang, Vice representative of the Chapei Police
Denny Tung Teing, Chairman of the Reception Committee; Daung
Koch Sang, Vice Chairman of the Reception Committee; Tsang T'u
Kyi, Chief of the National Salvation Army; Wong Hing, Deputy
Chief of the National Salvation Army; and Lau Ta Yong and Sih
En ng Jon who read the memorial service.

The service passed off without untoward incident and all
the guests together with the squad of special police from the
Bureau of Public Safety had left the premises by 12.00 noon.

[Signature]
D.D.C."C"
C.I.C Special Branch.

[Signature]
D. S. I.

West Hongkew Station,
REPORT
Date May 24th 19 3

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation.

Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
At 1.15 p.m. May 23, the Shanghai North Station area
and north of the railway track including Paoshan Road was evacu-
ated by Japanese forces and formerly handed over to the Chinese
Authorities. The area consists of the former 5th Police District
and No.2/5 Sub-Station. The area to the east of Paoshan Road
hitherto controlled by 1 and 2 Sub-Stations 5th District, will
continue to remain under Japanese jurisdiction for the time
being. No untoward incident occured during the process of
handing over.

At 4 p.m. on the Authority of the Defence Committee the
barbed wire on the north side of Boundary Road at the corner of
Cunningham Road was cut in order to give access to railway
employees from the Settlement to the North Station. The
opening was closed at 6.30 p.m. by the railway police and will
be opened today at the same time as other boundary gates.

[Signature]
D. S. I.

D.D.O."G"
O.i/c Special Branch.

5月23日下午1时15分，日军撤出上海北站区域及铁路轨道以北包括宝山路在内的地区，并正式移交给中国当局。该区域由原第五巡捕房辖区及第2/5分巡捕房组成。宝山路由东的区域，此前由第五巡捕房第1和第2分巡捕房管辖，目前将继续暂时处于日本管辖之下。移交过程中未发生意外事件。

West Hongkew Station,
REPORT
Date May 17th 1932

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation.

Made by D.S.I. G ash. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
Partial evacuation of Chapei by Japanese forces.
At 8 a.m. May 16, the Japanese forces evacuated that portion of Chapei bounded by the railway track on the north, by the Soochow Creek on the west and south and on the east by a li formed by the Chapei-Settlement Boundary from the Soochow Creek north to North Chekiang and Boundary Roads corner and continuing direct north to the railway track. The latter boundary is designated by a barbed wire barricade recently erected by the Japanese forces.
Consistent with the evacuation, the Municipality of Greater Shanghai resumed administration and the Bureau of Public Safety are policing the area. Divisional Headquarters have been established at Kong Woo Road and Sub. Stations at Mengku Road and Meiyuen Road.
The Shanghai North Station, the railway track and the area north and east of the above boundary will continue to be under Japanese jurisdiction for the time being.

No untoward incident was reported in the West Hongkew District during the day.
Refugees:- Details submitted on enclosed form.

[Signature]
D. S. I.

DIRECTOR.
O.I/C Special Branch.
[Signature]

先生，
日军部分撤离闸北。
1932年5月16日上午8时，日军撤出闸北以下区域：北至铁路轨道，西及南至苏州河，东至一条由苏州河向北延伸至浙江北路与边界路转角、并继续直向北至铁路轨道的闸北-租界界线所形成的线。后一界线以日军最近架设的铁丝网障碍物为标志。
随着撤离行动，大上海市政府恢复行政管理，公安局正在对该区域进行治安巡逻。分区指挥部已设在孔武路（Kong Woo Road），分巡捕房设在孟古路（Mengku Road）和梅园路（Meiyuen Road）。
上海北站、铁路轨道以及上述界线以北和以东的区域，目前仍将继续处于日本管辖之下。

Date May 9th 1932

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation.

Made by D.S.I. Gasn. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
Assistance to Japanese Naval Police.

At 2.15 a.m. on the May 9, 1932 one named K. Matsutani,
Japanese subject, accompanied by J.D.C. No.10, Hongke Station,
C.P.O. Minami and 6 members of the Japanese Naval Police,
came to this Station and asked for assistance to make inquiries
at No. 81 Elgin Road where the 1st named person alleged he had
been illegally detained and refused permission to remove his
effects from the room he was occupying. Necessary assistance
was rendered and it was ascertained that the tenant of the
house had been under the impression that the above named
was a Cantonese, but upon discovering that he was Japanese,
she ordered him to remove. He assumed a threatening attitude and
the tenant became afraid and locked him in the room. He later
escaped through a back window and reported the matter to the
Japanese Naval Headquarters.

Naval Police did not enter the premises. Property removed
in the presence of Police. No untoward incident occurred during
the removal.

Refugees. Details submitted on enclosed form.

[Signature]
D.D.O. "C"
O.i/c Special Branch.

West Hongkew Station,
REPORT
Date 1st May 1932.

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation.

Made by D.S.I. Gaskin Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
At 1.00 p.m. April 30, one named Yien Tsu Hyien (奚兆南)
residing at 170 Jehol Road was walking west to east on the south
side of Haining Road, when just east of Jehol Road he was called
upon to stop by Japanese marines who were patrolling on the
Chapei side of Haining Road. He did so, but then turned south
into an alleyway, one of the marines then mounted the wire
entanglements entered the Settlement, arrested him, and escorted
him to the local Japanese Headquarters on Ningku Road where, after
being questioned and struck several times by the marines he was
allowed to go. Enquiries in the vicinity show that as the Chinese
was dressed in foreign clothing the Japanese had mistaken him for
a Korean.
Witnessed by Privates Leach and Small of the 31st Infantry and
Municipal Police.
Statement of informant also verified by enquiries made in the
vicinity.

At 9.20 p.m. April 30, persons representing the house tenants
residing North of the Elgin Road, held a meeting in the Nanyang
Lodging House (南洋), North Chakiang Road, and discussed the
payment of house rent and Municipal taxes during the period of
hostilities.
The meeting decided to request the landlords to remit a months
house rent and also to try and avoid payment of Municipal taxes.
Meeting quite orderly and dispersed at 10.15 p.m.

References Details submitted on attached form.

(批：See also File C6103.)

[Signature]
C. 1/C, Special Branch

先生，
4月30日下午1时，一名名为 Yien Tsu Hyien (奚兆南)、居住于热河路170号的人士，在海宁路南侧由西向东行走，当行至热河路以东时，被在海宁路闸北一侧巡逻的日本海军陆战队士兵喝令停止。他照做了，但随即向南转入一条弄堂，其中一名士兵攀越铁丝网障碍进入租界，将其逮捕，并护送至宁古路（Ningku Road）当地的日本司令部，在经过讯问并被海军陆战队士兵殴打数次后，获准离开。经在附近调查，由于该中国人穿着西式服装，日本人误以为他是朝鲜人。
目击者为第31步兵团的 Leach 和 Small 二等兵以及工部局警察。
举报人的陈述也经附近调查得到核实。

4月30日晚上9时20分，代表爱而近路（Elgin Road）以北住户的人员在南洋旅社（南洋），北浙江路，举行会议，讨论战事期间的房租和市政税缴纳问题。
会议决定请求房东免除一个月房租，并试图避免缴纳市政税。
会议秩序井然，于晚上10时15分散会。

Date 30th April 1932.

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation.

Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by [签名]

Sir,
Following the Hongkew Park bomb outrage, the Japanese authorities yesterday afternoon closed all entrances from this district to Chapei and posted notices to this effect.
In consequence of this action a message was received from C.P.C. 3099 to effect that some trouble had occured between some members of the 31st U. S. Infantry and Japanese marines at Haining and North Thibet Roads corner. A party of police under Insp. Clissold attended and ascertained that at about 1.50 p.m. two Japanese marines entered the Settlement at this point and when challenged by two 31st sentries, pointed to some notices which they carried and intimated that they wished to post same on the walls.
They were permitted to post a notice at gate '13' and were then directed by the Americans to move back to the passage way in the barbed wire and out of the Settlement. At this movement an obstinate Chinese youth attempted to crawl through the wire and enter Chapei and intending to assist the Japanese marine in removing the Chinese, Pte McNamera one of the 31st sentries, is alleged to have struck the Japanese sentinel on the head. A scuffle ensued and the Americans who had by this time been joined by another patrol withdrew from the wire on the approach of Japanese reinforcements but Pte McNamera was forcibly detained by the Japanese. During the discussion that followed which was considerably handicapped through the inability of the Japanese officer to speak English, the Japanese assumed a threatening on guard position and it is alleged that bayonet thrusts were made. Later, the Japanese officer apparently realizing that it was all an accident, released Pte. McNamera.
The D.O. 'C' Div. attended and the incident was amicably

（左侧批注：C.P. / Am.B. / D.C. / 30 APR 1932 / [签名] / 3/4）

先生，

由于这一行动，中央电话交换台（C.P.C.）3099 传来消息，称美国步兵第31团的部分成员与日本海军陆战队员在海宁路与北西藏路转角处发生了一些纠纷。由 Clissold 巡官率领的一队警员前往现场，查明约在下午1时50分，两名日本海军陆战队员在此处进入租界，当受到两名第31团哨兵的盘查时，他们指了指随身携带的一些告示，示意希望将其张贴在墙上。
他们获准在13号门张贴了一张告示，随后被美方人员指示退回到铁丝网内的通道并离开租界。在此举动期间，一名固执的中国青年试图爬过铁丝网进入闸北，据称第31团哨兵之一 McNamera 二等兵意在协助日本海军陆战队员将该中国人带走时，击打了日本哨兵的头部。随即发生扭打，此时另一巡逻队已加入美方行列，但在日军增援部队逼近时，美国人从铁丝网处撤离，而 McNamera 二等兵被日军强行扣留。在随后的交涉中，由于日本军官不会说英语，沟通受到极大阻碍，日军摆出具有威胁性的警戒姿态，据称还进行了刺刀捅刺。后来，日本军官显然意识到这完全是一场意外，释放了 McNamera 二等兵。
“C”分区值班警官到场，事件得以友好

（左侧批注：C.P. / Am.B. / D.C. / 1932年4月30日 / [签名] / 3/4）

REPORT
Date 30th April 1932.

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation.

Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
Following the Hongkew Park bomb outrage, the Japanese authorities yesterday afternoon closed all entrances from this district to Chapei and posted notices to this effect.
In consequence of this action a message was received from C.P.C. 3099 to effect that some trouble had occured between some members of the 31st U. S. Infantry and Japanese marines at Haining and North Thibet Roads corner. A party of police under Insp. Clissold attended and ascertained that at about 1.50 p.m. two Japanese marines entered the Settlement at this point and when challenged by two 31st sentries, pointed to some notices which they carried and intimated that they wished to post same on the walls.
They were permitted to post a notice at gate #13# and were then directed by the Americans to move back to the passage way in the barbed wire and out of the Settlement. At this movement an obstinate Chinese youth attempted to crawl through the wire and enter Chapei and intending to assist the Japanese marine in removing the Chinese, Pte McNamara one of the 31st sentries, is alleged to have struck the Japanese sentinel on the head. A scuffle ensued and the Americans who had by this time been joined by another patrol withdrew from the wire on the approach of Japanese reinforcements but Pte McNamara was forcibly detained by the Japanese. During the discussion that followed which was considerably handicapped through the inability of the Japanese officer to speak English, the Japanese assumed a threatening on guard position and it is alleged that bayonet thrusts were made. Later, the Japanese officer apparently realizing that it was all an accident, released Pte. McNamara.
The D.O. 'C' Div. attended and the incident was amicably

先生，
继虹口公园炸弹暴行之后，日本当局于昨日下午关闭了从本区通往闸北的所有入口，并张贴告示以此示众。
由于这一行动，中央电话交换台（C.P.C.）3099 传来消息，称美国步兵第31团的部分成员与日本海军陆战队员在海宁路与北西藏路转角处发生了一些纠纷。由 Clissold 巡官率领的一队警员前往现场，查明约在下午1时50分，两名日本海军陆战队员在此处进入租界，当受到两名第31团哨兵的盘查时，他们指了指随身携带的一些告示，示意希望将其张贴在墙上。
他们获准在#13#号门张贴了一张告示，随后被美方人员指示退回到铁丝网内的通道并离开租界。在此举动期间，一名固执的中国青年试图爬过铁丝网进入闸北，据称第31团哨兵之一 McNamara 二等兵意在协助日本海军陆战队员将该中国人带走时，击打了日本哨兵的头部。随即发生扭打，此时另一巡逻队已加入美方行列，但在日军增援部队逼近时，美国人从铁丝网处撤离，而 McNamara 二等兵被日军强行扣留。在随后的交涉中，由于日本军官不会说英语，沟通受到极大阻碍，日军摆出具有威胁性的警戒姿态，据称还进行了刺刀捅刺。后来，日本军官显然意识到这完全是一场意外，释放了 McNamara 二等兵。
