SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. M. 155.
West Hongkew Station,
REPORT
Date 2nd April 1932.

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation and State of District.

Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

As a result of the decision to resume business, a general indication of the desire to return to normal conditions was noticeable throughout the West Hongkew district during the day. The majority of the shops which had hitherto conducted their business through pigeon holes or half closed doors were seen to be wide open and residents continue to return to their evacuated homes.

A further batch of 11 wounded soldiers were discharged from the 38th British Red Cross Hospital, Temple of Queen of Heaven and conveyed to Nantao by motor truck at 1.30 p.m. April 1. A total of 75 are now receiving treatment at this hospital. No further casualties were received during the day.

During the forenoon the 31st U. S. Infantry were relieved of their duties at the barricades and various defence positions in this district by a unit of the 2nd Batt. East Lancs Regt. The taking over of all posts was completed at 11 a.m.

Refugees. Details submitted on separate form.
Missing. None reported.

[Signature]
D. S. I.

D.D.C. "C"

O. i/c, Special Branch.

Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

"Citizens Federation", 15th Branch Activities.

During the day copies of the attached pamphlet urging the non-payment of rent and Municipal Rates issued jointly by the 15th Branch, Citizens Federation and the Soochow Road Merchants Union, were distributed to all shops on North Shanse Road together with copies of the poster "Put up a lengthy resistance; bear the pain and resume business". A subscription fee of 20 cents was paid by the majority of the shop-keepers to the person distributing this printed matter and in return a separate receipt was given for the amount received. - Specimen receipt attached.

The address of the 15th Branch Office is 31a East Tuh An Lee, off North Shanse Road. President's name:- Tsok Ts Zung (祝志纯).

A further batch of 5 wounded soldiers were discharged from the 38th Branch Red Cross Hospital, Temple of Queen of Heaven, and transported to Chinkiang by steamer at 2 p.m. March 31. A total of 91 are now receiving treatment at this institution. No further casualties were received during the day.

Refugees. Submitted on separate form.
Missing. None reported.

D. S. I.

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation and State of District.

Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by W Robertson Insp

Sir,
Throughout the day until dusk large numbers of Japanese naval and military reinforcements on foot and in motor trucks together with field guns, general equipment and supplies were seen to pass along Boundary Road and proceed west. Japanese in plain clothes were also observed accompanying the transports.
At 5 p.m. March 8, a 31st U.S. Infantry patrol escorted to this Station three Japanese civilians whom they had rescued from a hostile mob of Chinese on Kaifeng Road. They stated that a fourth had run off pursued by part of the crowd and was probably lost in some of the nearby alleyways. A party of Police immediately proceeded and searched the whole area without result. It was learned that people in the vicinity had seen him running towards Kansuh Road.
The three who had been rescued were escorted to Hongkew Stn and the following particulars of them obtained:-
Names, I. Takaoka, age 44, 105 Nanzing Road, K. Tajima, age 40, 105 Nanzing Road, A. Gato, age 32, 107 Pearson Road and M. Chida age 28, 105 Nanzing Road.
They stated that they were charcoal dealers and were seeking a place where they could purchase coke. At Winchester and Kaifeng Road corner they met C.P.C. 1626 whom they allege stopped them and struck the first named on his leg with his baton. A crowd quickly gathered and attacked them, members of the U.S. Infantry then came on the scene and rescued the first three named whilst the fourth ran off.
At about 5.30 p.m. a mobile party of Japanese Military consisting of an officer in charge of several men mounted on two motor cycle combinations carrying machine guns followed by another

全天直至黄昏，可见大量日本海军及军事增援部队徒步或乘坐卡车，连同野战炮、通用装备和物资，沿界路向西行进。还观察到便衣日本人随同运输车队行动。
3月8日下午5时，美国步兵第31团的一支巡逻队将三名日本平民护送至本巡捕房，他们是从开封路上充满敌意的中国暴民手中被救出的。他们称，第四人被部分人群追赶逃跑，可能迷失在附近的某条弄堂里。一队警察立即前往并搜索了整个区域，但无结果。据悉，附近有人看见他向甘肃路方向跑去。
获救的三人被护送至虹口巡捕房，并获取了以下详细信息：
姓名：I. Takaoka，44岁，南京路105号；K. Tajima，40岁，南京路105号；A. Gato，32岁，皮尔逊路（Pearson Road）107号；以及 M. Chida，28岁，南京路105号。
他们声称自己是煤炭经销商，正在寻找购买焦炭的地方。在温切斯特路（Winchester）与开封路路口，他们遇到了华捕第1626号，据称该警员拦住他们并用警棍击打了第一人的腿部。人群迅速聚集并攻击他们，随后美国步兵成员赶到现场救出了前三人，而第四人则逃跑了。

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation and State of District.
Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by W Robertson Insp
Sir,
With residents returning to their homes the greater number
of which have been evacuated since the commencement of hostilities
and shop keepers resuming business, further signs of returning
to normal conditions were noticeable throughout the West Hongkew
district during the day.
At 10.20 a.m. March 7, one Wong Tse Ching (王子卿 ),
manager of the North Station Hotel, No.5 Boundary Road reported
that on returning to inspect the above premises with a view to
resuming business, he discovered an unexploded shell in a bucket
of water on the ground floor. The projectile was found as stated
concealed in muddy water in a shadowed corner near the back
entrance and therefore could not have been seen by members of
the various defense units who have made use of this building
as an observation post. The shell which is of similar type
and calibre to those which have fallen in the district on previous
occasions was brought to the Station where it is now detained
pending instructions. It is assumed that the shell was found
in the vicinity of the hotel by a member of the defense forces
and placed in water for safety as there was no evidence of its
having fallen on the building or the adjacent premises.
No further casualties were received during the day at the
38th Branch Red Cross Hospital, Temple of Queen of Heaven, North
Honan Road.
Refugees. Details submitted on separate form.
Missing. None reported.
M. Gash.
D. S. I.

由副督察长 Gash 撰写。由 W Robertson 督察转呈
先生，
随着居民返回家园（其中大多数自敌对行动开始以来已撤离），且店主恢复营业，全天在西虹口区范围内可注意到进一步恢复正常状态的迹象。
3月7日上午10时20分，界路5号北站旅馆经理王子卿（Wong Tse Ching）报告称，他在返回上述处所视察以准备恢复营业时，在一楼的一桶水中发现了一枚未爆炸的炮弹。正如所述，该炮弹被发现隐藏在靠近后门的阴暗角落里的浑水中，因此曾将该建筑用作观察哨的各防御单位成员不可能看到它。这枚炮弹的类型和口径与该地区此前落下的炮弹相似，已被带至巡捕房，目前暂扣待命。推测这枚炮弹是由一名防御部队成员在旅馆附近发现并放入水中以确保安全，因为没有证据表明它落在该建筑或相邻处所上。
当天，位于北河南路天后宫的第38红十字分会医院未接收更多伤亡人员。
难民。详情另表提交。
失踪。无报告。
M. Gash。
副督察长
“C”区副总监。
特别课主管。

Subject (in full) State of emergency - Daily Observation and State of District.
Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by W Robertson Insp

Sir,
A general indication of the desire in business circles to return to normal conditions was noticeable throughout the West Hongkew district during the day. With the P.W.D. coolies engaged on removing the second line barbed wire, the shop keeping class is gradually gaining confidence and more shops are being opened that had hitherto conducted their business through pigeon holes in the shutters or half closed doors. A great number of residents were seen to be reoccupying their homes which they evacuated at the commencement of hostilities. On March 5, No. 5 route motor omnibuses extended their run as far north as Purdon Road Market.
At 10 a.m. two motor trucks conveying Japanese bluejackets approached the Haining Road barricade from Chapei, but upon seeing the gate closed and that they could not enter returned. A large number of Chinese who were waiting on the Settlement side of the barrier, on seeing the arrival of the Japanese became frightened and a mild panic ensued during which several persons received minor injuries as the result of being entangled in the barbed wire. The confusion subsided following the departure of the trucks and the arrival of additional Police.
No further casualties were received during the day at the 38th Branch Red Cross Hospital, Temple of Queen of Heaven.
Refugees. Details submitted on separated form.
Missing. None reported.

D. S. I.
D.D.O. "G"
O. i/c, Special Branch.

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation and state of District.
Made by D.S.I. Ga he. Forwarded by W. Robertson Insp
Sir,
During the day Japanese bluejackets patrolling the area in
the vicinity of the North Station were seen to be taking strict
precautions against looting following the evacuation of this area.
All Chinese that ventured into the sector were subjected to a
careful search and only Japanese civilians were allowed to move
about unmolested.
Large numbers of refugees continued to pour into the Settle-
ment from Chapei through the western entrances of this district
that were open for periods during the day. Precautions were
taken against looting and a total number of 125 arrests were made
at these points of persons suspected of being in possession of
stolen property. Of this total no less than 43 persons male and
female were charged in connection with 36 cases during the day.
At 1.30 p.m. a motor truck driven by a Japanese with another
Japanese and five Russian labourers as passengers in the vicinity
of the S.S.D. Court on Kansuh Road, was attacked by a crowd of
Chinese. The windscreen of the vehicle was broken and engine damaged.
None of the occupants were injured due to the intervention on the
part of members of the 31st U.S. Inf. The police arrived shortly
afterwards and the truck was escorted to Hongkew district and
handed over to a Japanese Patrol. The truck was hired by Mr.
Nishide, chemist of Woosung Road for the purpose of conveying
alcohol from a godown to his place of business.
At 6.20 p.m. one named Voong Zu Tsung (馮傳貞) a Chinese
river pilot residing at 434 Tsapee Road was brought to this Station
after having been rescued by the police from a crowd of Chinese
who having mistaken him for a Japanese, were chasing him on North
Shanse Road near the Tong Dong Ka Loong. Following his arrival

先生，
日间，可见日本水兵在北站附近区域巡逻，并在该区域疏散后采取严格措施防止抢劫。所有冒险进入该区域的中国人均受到仔细搜查，仅允许日本平民自由行动而不受干扰。

大量难民继续通过本区西部入口从闸北涌入租界，这些入口在日间部分时段开放。为防止抢劫采取了预防措施，在这些地点共逮捕了125名涉嫌持有赃物的人。其中，当天共有不少于43名男女因涉及36起案件而被起诉。

下午1时30分，一辆由一名日本人驾驶、载有另一名日本人和五名俄国劳工的卡车，在甘肃路特区法院附近遭到一群中国人的袭击。车辆挡风玻璃破碎，引擎受损。由于美国步兵第31团成员的干预，车内人员均未受伤。警察随后不久抵达，卡车被护送至虹口区并移交给日本巡逻队。该卡车系吴淞路化学师 Nishide 先生租用，用于将酒精从仓库运至其营业场所。

下午6时20分，一名名为 Voong Zu Tsung（馮傳貞）的中国引水员，居住于乍浦路434号，在被警察从一群中国人手中救出后被带至本巡捕房。这群人误以为他是日本人，正在通东卡龙附近的北山西路上追赶他。在他抵达

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation and State of District.

Made by D.S.I. Cash. Forwarded by W N Robertson Insp.

Sir,
At 8 a.m. March 3, the Japanese Imperial flag was hoisted over
the south wing of the North Station building where bluejackets
appear to have established headquarters for the detachments
patrolling that area. Throughout the day until dusk reinforce-
ments both naval and military on foot and in motor trucks and
waggons, field guns, general equipment and supplies were seen to
pass along Boundary Road in a westerly direction. A large number
of Japanese in plain clothes were also observed to accompany the
transports.
At 3 p.m. a motor truck conveying a number of Japanese troops
and supplies accompanied by a British military officer (name or
Regt. unknown) approached the Settlement side of the Kaifeng Road
boundary gate and requested to be allowed to pass through into
Chapel. Members of the U.S. 31st Inf. Regt. on duty at this
post refused to open the barricade and in the presence of Inspr.
Porritt S.M.P. (S) advised them to enter via Haining and North
Szechuen Road route, which they did.
Japanese troops were seen during the day establishing them-
selves in No. 1. - 4th Div. Chapel Police Station situated on
Mengku Road (continuation of Kaifeng Road). Chinese coolies were
seen to be working with them apparently without coercion.
Large numbers of refugees who had become terror stricken at
the sight of the Japanese troops searching for snipers, entered
the Settlement through the Kaifeng Road gate which was kept open
until 1 p.m. instead of 11 a.m. as usual.
At 4.55 p.m. a coolie named Tseu Yao Chi (周耀其), 30 M.P.A.
was brought to the station suffering from injuries to his face and
scalp as the result of being assaulted by a number of persons. It

由副督察长 Cash 撰写。由 W N Robertson 督察转呈。

先生，
3月3日上午8时，日本帝国国旗在北站建筑南翼升起，日本水兵似乎已在此为巡逻该区域的分队设立总部。全天直至黄昏，可见海军和军事增援部队徒步或乘坐卡车及货车，以及野战炮、一般装备和补给品沿界路向西行进。还观察到大量便衣日本人随同运输车队行动。

下午3时，一辆运送多名日本士兵和补给的卡车，由一名英国军官（姓名或团级不详）陪同，接近开封路边界门的租界一侧，请求允许穿过进入 Chapel（音译）。在此岗位执勤的美国步兵第31团成员拒绝打开路障，并在上海公共租界警务处（S）Porritt 督察的在场建议下，告知他们经由海宁路和北四川路路线进入，他们照此办理。

日间可见日本军队在位于孟古路（开封路延伸段）的第1-4师 Chapel（音译）警察局内驻扎。可见中国苦力与他们一起工作，显然未受胁迫。

大量难民因目睹日本军队搜寻狙击手而惊恐万分，通过开封路大门进入租界，该门保持开放至下午1时，而非通常的上午11时。

下午4时55分，一名名为 Tseu Yao Chi（周耀其）的苦力，30 M.P.A.（原文不清），因遭多人殴打致面部和头皮受伤，被带至巡捕房。据

was learned that his assailants had seen him, earlier in the
afternoon, working for the Japanese troops in the vicinity of
the North Station and on entering the Settlement had followed
him to the Tong Dong Ka Loong where at 3.30 p.m. they set upon
him. His condition is not serious and was not detained in
hospital.

At 5.15 p.m. information was received that residents on
Boundary Road and in the area north of Elgin Road were fearful
of being molested by the newly arrived Japanese troops and plain
clothes men. All available detectives were detailed to broadcast
the information that there was no danger and to reassure them that
they were quite safe. The mild panic subsided and residents
gained confidence when it was seen that Chinese were going about un-
molested by Japanese bluejackets on Boundary Road and in fact
were showing a desire to be friendly.

During the afternoon the Argyll and Sutherland Highlanders were
relieved of their duties at the barricades and various defence
positions in this district by the 31st U. S. Infantry. The
taking over of all posts was completed at 4 p.m.

During the day an additional 54 wounded Chinese troops were
received at the 38th Branch Red Cross Hospital, Temple of Queen
of Heaven. These casualties who were transferred from the
Nanyang Hospital, (南洋医院) Nantao, now being the total being treated
at this branch to 140.

Missing. None reported.

D. S. I.

下午5时15分，收到消息称，界路及爱而近路以北地区的居民担心受到新抵达的日本军队和便衣人员的骚扰。所有可用的侦探均被派去广播信息，称没有危险，并向他们保证他们非常安全。轻微的恐慌平息，当居民看到中国人在界路上自由行动而未受日本水兵干扰，且实际上表现出友好意愿时，他们恢复了信心。

下午期间，阿盖尔和萨瑟兰高地人团在本区的路障及各防御阵地的勤务由美国步兵第31团接替。所有岗位的交接于下午4时完成。

日间，另有54名受伤中国士兵被送往位于天后宫的第38支会红十字会医院。这些伤员是从南市南洋医院转移过来的，使得在该支会接受治疗的总数达到140人。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. M. 121.
West Hongkew Station,
REPORT
Date 3-3-32 19 .
Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation and State of District.
Made by D.S.I. Jash. Forwarded by W Robertson Insp.
Sir,
As the result of the advance made by Japanese outposts
across the Northern sector of Paoshan Road during the night of
Feb. 29, which exposed the Chinese positions on the southern
sections to an enfilading movement and thereby rendering their
strong defence barricades valueless, Chinese troops in this
sector commenced to retreat in a westerly direction at 6 a.m.
and by 9.30 a.m. had completely evacuated the North Station.
From points of vantage in this district the retreating forces
were seen to be leaving their positions in an orderly manner
but appeared to be badly shaken as the result of the recent aerial
and artillery bombardments. No reports have so far been received
of any attempt by them to enter or break through the Settlement.
Chinese field and trench mortar batteries continued to fire
intermittently apparently with the object of covering their retreat
and several fires were seen to break out in the direction of their
withdrawal which, it is presumed were started by them for the
same purpose. These fires spread very rapidly and within a few
hours had merged into one conflagration which was estimated to
cover an area of one and a half square miles.
At 4.30 p.m. with the assistance of a tank which made its
appearance at the rear of blockhouse 'B', an advance party of some
20 Japanese bluejackets left the protection of their barricades
and advanced along Boundary Road to blockhouse 'C'. Here they
halted whilst reinforcements accompanied by plain clothes men
entered the North Station and after completing a search of adjacent
buildings, placed a machine gun on the summit of the Station
building.
The Japanese advance moved with apparent rapidity for at

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案号 M. 121。
西虹口巡捕房，
报告
日期 1932年3月3日。
主题（全称）紧急状态 - 每日观察及辖区状况。
由副督察长 Jash 撰写。由 W Robertson 督察转呈。
先生，
由于2月29日夜間日本前哨阵地越过宝山路北部区域推进，使中国军队在南部地段的位置暴露于侧射火力之下，从而使其坚固的防御路障失去价值，该区域的中国军队于上午6时开始向西撤退，并于上午9时30分完全撤离北站。从本区的有利位置观察，撤退部队有序地离开阵地，但似乎因最近的空袭和炮击而受到严重震撼。迄今未收到任何关于他们试图进入或突破租界的报告。

中国军队的野战炮和战壕迫击炮连继续间歇性射击，显然是为了掩护其撤退，并在其撤退方向观察到多处起火，推测也是出于同样目的由他们点燃。这些火势蔓延极快，几小时内汇成一片大火，估计覆盖面积达一平方英里半。

下午4时30分，在一辆出现在碉堡“B”后方的坦克协助下，约20名日本水兵的先遣队离开路障的保护，沿界路推进至碉堡“C”。在此他们暂停，与此同时，伴随便衣人员的增援部队进入北站，在完成对相邻建筑物的搜查后，在车站建筑顶部架设了一挺机枪。

日军的推进看似迅速，因为

on the railway track one mile west of the North station and
no opposition had been met with. At 7.30 p.m. about 200
reinforcements accompanied the team along the Boundary Road to
'G' blockhouse where it remained during the night which passed

The fires showed no sign of subsiding and, at 6 a.m. March

黄昏时分，据报道先遣队已到达北站以西一英里的铁轨处，且未遭遇抵抗。晚上7时30分，约200名增援部队沿界路陪同该小队至“G”碉堡，并在那里过夜，夜间除了来自北方远处的猛烈枪声外，一切平静。

火势未见减弱迹象，至3月3日上午6时，已蔓延至车站稍西处的铁路北侧。可见日本水兵正在将已撤离的沙袋工事改为己用。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. M. 1184
REPORT
At Hongkew Station,
Date 2-3-32. 19

Subject (in full) State of emergency - Daily Observation and State of District.

Made by D.S.I. Cash. Forwarded by W.N. Johnston Insp.

Sir,
Except for a short period between 2 p.m. and 2.30 p.m. during which Japanese aircraft carried out a raid on positions immediately behind the Chinese lines in the vicinity of Jukong Road, the Paoshan Road Sector in the vicinity of the North Station was unusually quiet during the day. The land planes taking part in the raid appeared to concentrate their bombing at a point approximately one half mile north-west of the Commercial Press building in which locality batteries of Chinese field guns are believed to be situated. About six bombs which appeared to be incendiary, were dropped at this point and as a result a fire broke out. Aided by a southerly wind the fire spread rapidly in both northern and easterly directions. At 12.15 a.m. a second fire was seen to break out spontaneously at a point approximately 600 yards south west of the origin of the other fire and spread to adjacent buildings in a northerly direction. At 6 a.m. March 2, it was estimated that the conflagrations had destroyed an area from one half to three quarters of a mile square and showed little sign of subsiding.

On March 1, the Temple of Queen of Heaven, Chinese Chamber of Commerce building, North Honan Road was taken over by the 38th Branch Hospital of the China Red Cross Association and prepared for the reception of wounded Chinese soldiers. Dr. Koo Nan Chun (顧南羣) is in charge and so far accomodation has been made for 300 patients. Between 4 p.m. and 5 p.m. 86 casualties were received. These are reported to have come from the Kiangwan front.

At 6 a.m. March 2, Chinese troops were still in possession of the North Station and the relative position of their defences remains unchanged.

Missing. None reported.

D.D.O. "C"
O. i/c, Special Branch.

(签名: M. Cash. D.S.I.)

报告
虹口巡捕房，
日期 1932年3月2日。

主题（全称）紧急状态 - 每日观察及辖区状况。

由副督察长卡什（Cash）撰写。由约翰斯顿（W.N. Johnston）督察转发。

先生，
除下午2时至2时30分这一短暂时段内，日本飞机对北站附近朱恭路（Jukong Road）中国防线后方阵地实施空袭外，北站附近的宝山路防区在白天异常平静。参与空袭的陆基飞机似乎将轰炸集中在商务印书馆大楼西北约半英里处，据信该地部署有中国野战炮兵连。约有六枚看似燃烧弹的炸弹投掷在该点，导致火灾发生。在南风的助长下，火势迅速向北方和东方蔓延。凌晨12时15分，另一处火灾在距第一起火点西南约600码处自发燃起，并向北蔓延至邻近建筑物。截至3月2日上午6时，估计大火已摧毁了半平方英里至四分之三平方英里的区域，且几乎没有减弱的迹象。

3月1日，位于河南北路的天后宫及中国商会大楼被中国红十字会第三十八分院接管，并准备接收受伤的中国士兵。顾南羣医生负责此事，目前已安置300名伤员。下午4时至5时间，接收了86名伤员。据报这些伤员来自江湾前线。

3月2日上午6时，中国军队仍控制着北站，其防御阵地的相对位置保持不变。

失踪人员。无报告。

“C”处助理处长
特别科主管。

（签名：M. Cash. 副督察长）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
West Hongkew. Station,
File No. M./ 22.
REPORT
Date March 2nd. 1932
19

Subject (in full) Chinese civilian shot by Japanese Bluejackets in Chapei and
taken to the Red Cross Hospital, Avenue Haig, for treatment.

Made by D.S. Harvey. Forwarded by W. Robertson Insp.

Sir,
At 9-30pm 2-3-32 one, Yang Yung Kyi (楊鳳歧), manager of
the Shing Tah Ziang (兴泰祥) general goods store, 165 Singkiang
Road, Chapei, came to the station and reported that at 5-30pm
2-3-32 he saw a male Chinese, whom he knew, named Yei Ah Loh (易阿
六), age 18, native of Pootung, residing in the Ching Che Li (靖济
里) off Singkiang Road, Chapei, lying inside the latter alleyway
suffering from bullet wounds in the right leg and abdomen. Furth-
er that he, (Yang) obtained the assistance of some neighbours and
together they carried the injured man into the Yoong Ce Li (永庆里)
off N. Thibet Road. A member of the Argyll and Sutherland High-
landers was on duty nearby and it would appear that he was respons-
ible for calling the S.P.B. ambulance which subsequently removed
the injured man to the Red Cross Hospital, Avenue Haig.

Bubbling Well Station was requested to send a Chinese
detective to the Hospital who ascertained from the injured man
that at about 4pm 2-3-32 he, accompanied by three others were
walking East along Jukeng Road when they were called upon to
stop by about twelve Japanese Bluejackets. The four men became
afraid and commenced to run away whereupon the Bluejackets opened
fire bringing all four to the ground. The injured man (Yei) was,
after some time able to crawl along the ground and with the assis-
tance of some other male Chinese entered the alleyway inside which
he was found by the informant.

The Chinese detective attached to Bubbling Well was inform-
ed by the Hospital staff that the injured man was considered to
be in a serious condition.

(批：Chater)

D.S.
O. I/C Spec. Br.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
西虹口巡捕房，
档案号 M./ 22.
报告
日期 1932年3月2日

主题（全称）一名中国平民在闸北被日本水兵枪击，并被送往海格路红十字会医院接受治疗。

由侦探警员哈维（Harvey）撰写。由罗伯逊（W. Robertson）督察转发。

先生，
1932年3月2日晚9时30分，闸北新江路165号兴泰祥百货店经理杨凤歧（Yang Yung Kyi）来到巡捕房报告称，当日下午5时30分，他看见一名他认识的中国男子，名叫易阿六（Yei Ah Loh），18岁，浦东人，居住在闸北新江路靖济里，躺在该弄堂内，右腿和腹部受枪伤。此外，他（杨）获得了一些邻居的帮助，共同将伤者抬入北西藏路永庆里。当时附近有一名阿盖尔和萨瑟兰高地团（Argyll and Sutherland Highlanders）的士兵在执勤，似乎是他呼叫了工部局警车，随后将伤者送往海格路红十字会医院。

静安寺巡捕房奉派派遣一名华探前往医院，从伤者处获悉，1932年3月2日下午4时许，他与另外三人沿朱恭路向东行走时，被约十二名日本水兵喝令站住。四人因恐惧开始逃跑，随即水兵开火，将四人全部击倒。伤者（易）过了一段时间后能够在地面爬行，并在其他几名中国男子的帮助下进入弄堂，举报人即在此处发现了他。

静安寺巡捕房所属华探从医院工作人员处获悉，伤者情况被认为十分危急。

（批注：Chater）

侦探警员
特别科主管

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
West Hongkew Station,
REPORT
Date March 2nd 1932.

Subject (in full) Chinese soldiers' uniforms found inside an unoccupied house
situated inside an alleyway off Boundary Road.

Made by D.S. Harvey. Forwarded by W Robertson Insp

Sir,
At 8.10 p.m. 2-3-32 a telephone message was circulated to
the effect that members of the Argyll and Sutherland Highlanders
had found a number of Chinese officers uniforms inside an unoccu-
pied house off Boundary Road, and that some identification docu-
ments had been taken away by Captain Wilson Brand G.S.O. (Intelligen
ce).

D.S. Harvey interviewed Captain Anderson the adjutant of the
above regiment who stated that he could not definitely say how the
uniforms came to be there but suggested that they may have been
discarded by deserters from the 19th Route Army. Captain Anderson
handed over four tunics, six caps and one pair of puttees which are
now being detained in the station pending instructions being re-
ceived regarding the disposal of same.

D.S.
W.C.
Sen. Det.

D.D.O. "C".

O.i/c Special Branch.

西虹口巡捕房，
报告
日期 1932年3月2日。

主题（全称）在界路（Boundary Road）旁一条弄堂内的一栋无人居住的房屋内发现中国军服。

由侦探警员哈维（Harvey）撰写。由罗伯逊（W Robertson）督察转发

先生，
1932年3月2日晚8时10分， circulated 一通电话消息，大意是阿盖尔和萨瑟兰高地团的成员在界路旁一栋无人居住的房屋内发现了多套中国军官制服，部分身份证明文件已被威尔逊·布兰德（Wilson Brand）上尉（情报参谋军官）取走。

侦探警员哈维采访了上述团队的副官安德森（Anderson）上尉，他表示无法确切说明制服为何出现在那里，但推测可能是第十九路军逃兵丢弃的。安德森上尉移交了四件上衣、六顶帽子和一副绑腿，目前这些物品暂扣在巡捕房，等待关于如何处置的指示。

侦探警员
W.C.
高级侦探

“C”处助理处长。

特别科主管。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. M.
west Hongkew Station,
REPORT
Date 1-3-32. 19

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation and state of District.

Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by W Robertson Insp.

Sir,
Commencing at 8.45 a.m. Feb 29, and continuing until
12.30 p.m. an intensive bombardment was carried out on the
Chinese positions in the vicinity of the North Station. Japanese
howitzer and field pieces from the direction of Hongkew Park
appeared to concentrate their fire on the Paoshan Road, north of
Jukong Road whilst several aeroplanes assisted throughout the
morning and were seen to drop a great number of bombs on essential
positions immediately behind the Chinese lines and on the railway
track at Markham Road Station. The Chinese replied using stokes
mortars positioned a short distance north-west of the North
Station whilst a field battery which appeared to be in the vicini-
ty of Markham Road Station was seen to be in action.
After a brief lull three Japanese land planes re-appeared
over Chapei at 1.45 p.m. and were seen to drop a number of bombs
on Chinese positions situated a short distance north-west of the
Commercial Press building. As a result, a fire was seen to
break out and aided by a strong wind spread rapidly in a
westerly direction. At 1 a.m. the fire was observed to have
practically burned itself out and from points of vantage it was
estimated that an area covering one half mile had been destroyed.
At 7 p.m. the bombardment was renewed in the vicinity of
the Paoshan Road Sector. This continued intermittently until 10pm.
when it died down and remained quiet throughout the night.
At 6 a.m. March 1, Chinese troops were still in possession
of the North Station and the relative position of their defences
remains unchanged.

Casualties. Nil.
Missing. None reported.

D.D.O. "C".
O. i/c Special Branch.

(签名: M. Gash.)
D. S. I.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案号 M.
西虹口巡捕房，
报告
日期 1932年3月1日。

主题（全称）紧急状态 - 每日观察及辖区状况。

由副督察长加什（Gash）撰写。由罗伯逊（W Robertson）督察转发。

先生，
从2月29日上午8时45分开始，持续至中午12时30分，日军对北站附近的中国阵地进行了猛烈轰炸。来自虹口公园方向的日本榴弹炮和野战炮似乎集中火力轰击朱恭路以北的宝山路，同时几架飞机在整个上午提供支援，并在中国防线后方的重要阵地以及麦根路（Markham Road）车站的铁轨上投下了大量炸弹。中方使用位于北站西北不远处的斯托克斯迫击炮进行还击，同时观察到疑似位于麦根路车站附近的野战炮兵连也在行动。
经过短暂的停歇，三架日本陆基飞机于下午1时45分再次出现在闸北上空，并在中国商务印书馆大楼西北不远处的中国阵地上投下数枚炸弹。结果，引发火灾，并在强风助长下迅速向西蔓延。凌晨1时，观察到火势基本自行熄灭，从有利地形估计，受灾面积约为半平方英里。
晚上7时，宝山路防区附近重新遭到轰炸。这种轰炸断断续续持续到晚上10时，随后减弱，整夜保持平静。
3月1日上午6时，中国军队仍控制着北站，其防御阵地的相对位置保持不变。

伤亡人数。无。
失踪人员。无报告。

“C”处助理处长。
特别科主管。

（签名：M. Gash.）
副督察长

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. M. 116.
West Hongkew Station,
REPORT
Date 29-2-32 19
Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation and State of District.
Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by W Robertson Insp.
Sir,
Except for occasional short bursts of rifle and machine gun fire and distant reports of intermittent shelling, the Paoshan Road Sector in the vicinity of the North Station was comparatively quiet during the day Feb. 28.
Assisted by a strong wind the fire which broke out as the result of an aerial bombardment at 3 p.m. Feb. 27, continued to burn throughout the day and at 11.30 p.m. Feb. 28, had assumed such proportions that the extremities of the affected area were estimated to be almost one mile apart. From a point of vantage on Boundary Road the burned out portion of the district appears to be along Jukong Road west and east from Paoshan Road and not less than one half mile from the North Station. At 6 a.m. Feb. 29, the area west of Paoshan Road had burned out whilst flames were still to be seen at the eastern extremity apparently near North Szechuen Road Extension.
At 5.20 a.m. the Chinese positions along the Paoshan Road Sector and in the vicinity of the North Station were again subjected to a heavy bombardment by Japanese artillery believed to be the howitzer battery situated in Hongkew Park or Rifle Range. After firing several salvoes at intervals of a few minutes the shelling died down at 5.40 a.m. The Chinese troops along Paoshan Road then replied with intensive rifle and machine gun fire for a period of fifteen minutes.
Despite the heavy bombardment, the Chinese troops were still in possession of the North Station and the relative position of their defences remains unchanged at 6 a.m. Feb. 29.
Casualties. Nil.
Missing. None reported.
D.D.O. "C"
O. i/c, Special Branch.
D. S. I.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案号 M. 116.
西虹口巡捕房，
报告
日期 1932年2月29日
主题（全称）紧急状态 - 每日观察及辖区状况。
由副督察长加什（Gash）撰写。由罗伯逊（W Robertson）督察转发。
先生，
除偶尔短暂的步枪和机枪射击声以及远处间歇性的炮击声外，2月28日白天，北站附近的宝山路防区相对平静。
在强风助长下，2月27日下午3时空袭引发的火灾整天持续燃烧，截至2月28日晚上11时30分，火势规模巨大，估计受灾区域两端相距近一英里。从界路的一处有利观察点看，烧毁的区域似乎沿着朱恭路，从宝山路向西和向东延伸，距离北站不少于半英里。2月29日上午6时，宝山路以西的区域已烧毁，而在东端， apparently 靠近北四川路延伸段附近，仍可见火焰。
上午5时20分，沿宝山路防区及北站附近的中国阵地再次遭到日本火炮的猛烈轰炸，据信该炮兵连位于虹口公园或靶子场。在间隔几分钟发射数轮齐射后，炮击于上午5时40分减弱。随后，沿宝山路的中国军队以密集的步枪和机枪火力还击了十五分钟。
尽管遭受猛烈轰炸，截至2月29日上午6时，中国军队仍控制着北站，其防御阵地的相对位置保持不变。
伤亡人数。无。
失踪人员。无报告。

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation and State of District.

Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by W. Robertson Supt.

Sir,
Following the heavy shelling during the early morning
of Feb. 27, by Japanese howitzer batteries which are believed
to be positioned in Hongkew Park, the Chinese defences in the
vicinity of Paoshan Road were subjected to intermittent fire
from the same source throughout the day. In addition to the
fire which began during the previous night and which continued
burn throughout the day over a large area, another out-break
was seen at about 9 a.m. at a point about 200 yards north of
the North Honan Road Blockhouse on the east side of Paoshan
Road. This building which is reported to be the premises of a
linoleum factory burned throughout the day but showed no signs
of spreading towards the Settlement.
At 3 p.m. three Japanese land planes appeared over Chapel
and were seen to drop six bombs (some appeared to be incendiary)
in the vicinity of the Chinese positions at Paoshan and Jukong
Road corner. As a result, a third fire broke out at a point
estimated at a little less than a mile due north of the Railway
Station. Burning rapidly and assisted by a strong wind the
fire quickly spread in both east and westerly directions. At
6 a.m. Feb. 28, the fire had covered an area of approximately
a half a mile and was still burning.
At 12.20 a.m. Feb. 28, Japanese artillery, believed to
be the howitzer battery situated in Hongkew Park, opened fire
with salvoes at regular intervals of three or four minutes, on
the Chinese positions in the vicinity of the North Station and
Paoshan Road Sector. Several shells exploded in the Railway
Station compound west of the Station building. The bombardment
died down at 1 a.m. and only occasional bursts of machine gun

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation and State of District.

Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by W.N. Benton Insp.

Sir,
At 12.25 p.m. Feb. 26 information was received from Capt.
Kennedy that a sniper was operating in the vicinity of the North
Honan and Range Road barricade inside the Settlement. A party
of Police under S. I. Pike immediately proceeded to the scene and
from an interview with the officer in charge of the post it was
ascertained that at about 12 noon two shots, believed to be rifle
fire, were seen by a sentry to strike the East wall of a Chinese
dwelling house situated on the west side of North Honan Road
directly opposite the north-east corner of Range Road near the
barricade. The reports of the shots were heard to come from the
direction of houses situated on the north side of Range Road near
Fusan Road. These houses, it was pointed out by the Police are,
up to a point near the Blockhouse, occupied by Japanese troops and
it is therefore improbable, assuming that the alleged sniper were
a Chinese, that he would be active on the premises or conceal
himself therein. On the other hand it would be impossible for
a Japanese sniper to fire at Chinese troops in the North Station
from that side of the building and it is very unlikely that he
would deliberately fire at the troops on the North Honan Road
barricade.
It was therefore concluded that the shots were probably fired
either by accident or strays by the Japanese troops who are hold-
ing a sandbag position on Range Road near Fusan Road. In his
report, the officer stated, he would request that the Japanese
H. Q. be informed of the incident as the ground floor room of the
house that was struck is used as a billet for two men. No
further shots have been heard.

敬启者：
2月26日下午12时25分，接获 Kennedy 上尉通报，称有一名狙击手在租界内北河南路与靶子路（Range Road）路障附近活动。由警佐 Pike 率领的一队警员立即赶赴现场，经与该岗位负责军官面谈后查明，约在中午12时，一名哨兵看见两发疑似步枪射击的子弹击中位于北河南路西侧、正对靶子路东北角靠近路障处的一栋中国民宅的东墙。据闻枪声来自靶子路北侧靠近福生路（Fusan Road）的房屋方向。警方指出，这些房屋直至靠近碉堡（Blockhouse）附近的一处地点，均由日军占领，因此，假设所谓的狙击手为中国人，他不太可能在该处活动或藏身其中。另一方面，日本狙击手也不可能从建筑物的那一侧向北站的中国军队射击，而且他也不太可能故意向北河南路路障处的部队射击。

West Hongkew Station,
REPORT
Date 26-2-32 /9

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation and State of District.

Made by D.S.I. Cash. Forwarded by W. Robertson. Insp.

Sir,
Commencing at 10.30 a.m. February 25, and throughout the day, the shelling of the North Station and Paoshan Road area by heavy artillery continued intermittently with occasional bursts of machine gun fire. From points of vantage on Boundary Road three fresh outbreaks of fire were seen as a result of the bombardment within a radius of one mile, north of the Railway Station.
At 6.30 p.m. intensive machine gun, trench mortar and rifle fire broke out in the vicinity of the Paoshan Road Sector. This continued until 7.15 p.m. when it died down and but for occasional bursts of machine gun fire and intermittent reports of shelling remained quiet during the night.
At 6 a.m. February 26, the Chinese positions in and around the North Station were relatively unchanged. No shells are reported to have fallen in this district during the past 24 hours.
Military movements.
During the afternoon the 31st U.S. Infantry were relieved of their duties at the barricades and the various defence positions in this district by the Argyll and Sutherland Highlanders. The taking over of all posts was completed by 4 p.m.
Refugees. Details submitted on separated form.
Casualties. Nil.
Missing. None reported.

D. S. I.

D.D.O. "C".
O. i/c Special Branch.

由副督察长 Cash 呈报。经督察 W. Robertson 转呈。

敬启者：
自2月25日上午10时30分起，全天重型火炮对北站及宝山路地区的炮击断断续续进行，间或有机枪扫射。从界路（Boundary Road）上的有利观测点可见，炮击导致火车站以北一英里半径范围内发生三起新的火灾。
下午6时30分，宝山路地段附近爆发密集的机枪、战壕迫击炮和步枪火力。这种情况持续至晚上7时15分才减弱，除偶尔的机枪扫射和间歇性的炮击声外，夜间保持平静。

Sir,

This continued with intensity until 12.15 p.m. when it died down and only occasional bursts of machine gun fire were heard during the afternoon. From 5.20 p.m. to 5.40 p.m. four Japanese planes appeared over Chapei and were seen to drop approximately fifteen bombs in the vicinity of Paoshan Road about one mile north of the Railway Station.

At 7 p.m. trench mortar and machine gun fire again broke out in the vicinity of the North Station and continued with intensity. The bombardment died down at 7.30 p.m. but recommenced at 8.30 p.m. in the same sector and also adjacent areas until 9.15 p.m. only intermittent shelling accompanied by machine gun fire was then heard.

At 2.15 a.m. Feb. 25 Japanese artillery again opened fire on the Chinese positions in the vicinity of the North Station. Several shells dropped in the Railway Station compound west of the Station building and as a result a fire broke out in the remaining godowns which are situated but a few yards north of Boundary Road a short distance from the North Chekiang Road Block-house. The bombardment ceased at 2.45 a.m. but the fire continued to burn and finally engulfed the whole of the structure which was practically gutted at 6 a.m. Feb. 25. No Settlement property was affected.

Sir,
Commencing at 10.45 a.m. Feb. 22, and continuing for about two hours an intensive bombardment broke out from the Chinese lines in the vicinity of the North Station and Paoshan Road and adjacent areas. Three trench mortars assisted by two batteries of field guns were brought into action and from various positions a short distance to the North and West of the North Station fired incessantly in the direction of North Szechuen Road and Hongkew Park. The Japanese replied heavily apparently with howitzer batteries and several shells were seen to burst in the vicinity of the Commercial Press building and along Paoshan Road. The bombardment continued intermittently during the afternoon until 6.40 p.m. when heavy firing again broke out along this sector. This died down at 7.30 p.m. and it is reported that a Japanese infantry attack on the North Station was repulsed.

At 9.25 p.m. Chinese heavy guns, believed to be two in number, which are reported to be mounted on an armoured train were brought into action. These guns, the detonations from which were louder than have been heard hitherto, fired several rounds and the shells were distinctly heard to pass over this district in an easterly direction. The shelling ceased at 9.45 p.m. but again commenced at 11.40 p.m. continuing at intervals of less than a minute until 11.55 p.m. when it ceased fire. During the latter period from a point of vantage on the S.S.D. Court building, it is estimated that from the flash of these guns that their position when in action was west of Markham Road Railway Station. No further reports have been received of shells dropping in this district.

Sir,
At 12.30 p.m. Feb. 20, a shell believed to have come from a
North-easterly direction penetrated the roof and exploded inside
a Chinese dwelling house situated at No. 127 ung Heu Li, (存厚里)
Cunningham Road. At the time of the explosion two Chinese
females and a youth were on the ground floor of the premises.
The youth was killed instantly, one of the females received fatal
injuries and died on admittance to hospital whilst the other
female sustained a serious wound in the right foot. They were
immediately removed to The Lester Chinese Hospital. Their
particulars are as follows:-
Dao Chia Hsiang (陶嘉祥), age 14, Native
Nanking, Student S.M.C. Primary School for
Chinese - Killed. "Wound of chest & abdomen".
He is the son of:-
Dao Joo Sz (陶吴氏) 38, Female, Native
Nanking. "Wound of back". Died on admission
to Hospital.
Tsang Jong Sz (张王氏) 58, Suchow, Amah,
employed by above named. "Wound of right foot".
Detained in hospital.
It was learned from enquiries that the husband of the
deceased, one Dau Su Ying (陶士英) a translator employed by
Kraush & Co., 2 Peking Road now residing at No. 300 Sai Zung Fong
off Nyburgh Road evacuated the above premises with his family on
or about January 29, 1932. During the forenoon Feb. 20, his
wife together with her son and amah revisited the house for the
purpose obtaining the remainder of their property and during the
time they were so engaged the shell struck the premises. The

Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by W. Robertson. Insp.

Sir,
Following a comparatively quiet day during which only
occasional bursts of rifle and machine gun fire were heard, a
heavy artillery bombardment broke out at 6.45 p.m. in the vici-
nity of the North Station and continued intermittently until
11.45 p.m. From points of vantage on Boundary Road several
shells were seen to burst some distance north of the Railway
Station near Paoshan Road resulting in fresh outbreaks of fire
which continued to burn throughout the night.
Commencing at 12.30 a.m. until 1.10 a.m. February 19, a
Chinese battery consisting it is believed of three guns was
brought into action at a point near the railway track a short
distance west of the North Station platforms. These guns fired
several salvoes and the shells were distinctly heard to pass
over this district in an easterly direction.
No reports have so far been received of shells dropping in
this district.
Despite the heavy bombardment there was no change in the
position of the Chinese defences in around the North Station at
6 a.m. February 19.
Casualties. Nil.
Missing. None reported.

D. S. I.

Station and Paoshan Road sector. These areas except for
occasional bursts of rifle and machine gun fire were compara-
tively quiet during the day February 17.
At 7.30 a.m. F.P.S. Baker brought to Station an unexploded
shell which had penetrated a Chinese shoe shop No.256a North
Chekiang Road and embedded itself in the rear wall of the pre-
mises. Enquiries show that at about 4.15 a.m. Feb. 17 the
shell coming from a northerly direction first entered the roof
of a cigarettes shop situated at No.243 North Chekiang Road and
passing through a partition and a first floor window of the
adjacent premises (Yuen Woo 源和 Restaurant, No.240 North
Chekiang Road) ricocheted across the road and piercing the door
of the above shoe shop came to rest as stated. There were no
injuries and only slight damage was done to the premises
concerned.
At 6 a.m. February 18 the positions of the Chinese defences
in the vicinity of the North Station compound and Paoshan Road
were relatively unchanged.

S. Hongkew Station,
Date 17-2-32. 19

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation and State of Districts.

Made by D.S.I. Garde Forwarded by W Robertson Insp.

Sir,
Except for occasional bursts of rifle and machine gun fire
and intermittent reports of shell explosions the Paoshan Road
sector in the vicinity of the North Station was comparatively
quiet during the day February 16.
At 3 a.m. Feb. 17, an intensive bombardment by both Chinese
and Japanese artillery commenced on their respective fronts and
continued until 5 a.m. During the bombardment several shells
were heard to pass over this district and from points of vantage
some were seen to explode in the direction of Gordon Road and
Wayside districts respectively.
Prior to the bombardment under cover of darkness, Chinese
troops were seen to be strengthening their defensive positions.
A second line of defence consisting of wooden crates containing
pressed paper has now been erected in the North Station compound
to the right and parallel with the front wall of what now remains
of the Station building. During the past two nights barbed wire
has been effectively strung in front of the sandbag defences along
the Station road towards Paoshan Road. This position which is
now supported by two machine guns and automatic rifles appears to
be practically impregnable from an infantry attack.
The relative positions of these defences remains unchanged
at 6 a.m. Feb. 17. No further reports have been received of
shells or bombs dropping in the district.

Casualties. Nil.
Missing. None.

D. S. I.

D.D.O. "C".
O. i/c, Special Branch.

2月17日凌晨3时，中日双方 artillery 在各自战线开始密集炮击，持续至凌晨5时。炮击期间，听到数枚炮弹飞过本辖区上空，并从有利观察点看到一些炮弹分别在戈登路（Gordon Road）和韦斯特菲尔德（Wayside，音译）区域方向爆炸。

截至2月17日上午6时，这些防御阵地的相对位置保持不变。未收到关于炮弹或炸弹落入本辖区的进一步报告。

Sir,
At 5.15 p.m. rifle and machine gun fire accompanied
by a heavy artillery bombardment broke out in the vicinity
of the North Station. This continued with intensity until
8 p.m. when it died down somewhat and only occasional bursts
of machine gun fire were heard during the night. Prior to
this period the Paoshan Road sector was comparatively quiet
during the day February 15.

At 10 a.m. C.P.W.87 brought to the Station an unexploded
shell which the tenant, one named 'Yu' (俞 ) had discovered
in an upstairs front bedroom when revisiting his home for a
short period. Enquiries show that the shell coming from a
Northerly direction penetrated the wall and passing through
the back room came to rest in the front room. The premises
are occupied by the Bee Shing (義兴 ) Transportation Co. No.287 Elgin Road
of which the tenant is the proprietor. He has vacated the premi-
ses and cannot at present be located. No other damage was
done to the premises apart from the hole in the wall and
wooden partition. According to C.P.W.435, the shell struck
the premises at about 11 p.m. Feb. 13. No one was injured.

Another shell of the same calibre was brought to this
Station by Lt. Boyd 'B' Coy. S.V.C. which had been given him
by an unknown Chinese at the corner of Chekiang and Boundary
Roads. Enquiries show that the shell had dropped through
the roof of the Tsang Tah Cigarette shop situated at the
corner of North Chekiang and Boundary Roads and passing
through the floor came to rest in a small ground floor
back room. The premises are vacated and the tenants cannot
at present be located.

There was no one injured. Both Shells are detained

先生，
下午5时15分，北站附近爆发了伴随猛烈炮击的步枪和机枪火力。这种激烈战斗持续至晚上8时，随后势头稍减，夜间仅偶尔听到机枪火力爆发。在此之前，2月15日白天，宝山路区域相对平静。

上午10时，C.P.W.87将一枚未爆炮弹带至巡捕房，该炮弹是由一名姓“俞”（Yu）的租户在短暂回家查看时，在楼上的一间前卧室发现的。调查显示，这枚来自北方的炮弹穿透墙壁，穿过里屋，最终停在前屋。该处所由义兴（Bee Shing）运输公司占用，地址为埃尔金路287号，该租户即为业主。他已搬离该处所，目前下落不明。除墙壁和木隔板上的洞孔外，该处所未受其他损坏。据C.P.W.435称，炮弹击中该处所的时间约为2月13日晚上11时。无人受伤。

另一枚相同口径的炮弹由义勇军后备队（S.V.C.）B连连长博伊德（Boyd）中尉带至本巡捕房，该炮弹是一名身份不明的中国人在浙江路与界路转角处交给他的。调查显示，该炮弹落穿了位于浙江北路与界路转角处的藏达（Tsang Tah，音译）香烟店的屋顶，穿过地板，最终停在一楼的一个小后屋内。该处所已空置，租户目前下落不明。

无人受伤。两枚炮弹均扣留

Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by W N Robertson Insp.

Sir,
The shelling of the Chinese positions in the vicinity
of the North Station continued intermittently throughout the
day until 11.30 p.m. February 13. Between 8 a.m. and 9 a.m.
eight Japanese planes assisted in the bombardment, these
appeared to concentrate their bombing in the direction of
Markham Road Station. They dropped approximately fifteen
bombs which were of much louder detonation than have been
heard hitherto. As a result of the bombardment several fires
broke out and were seen burning throughout the night over a
large area north-west of the North Station.

Despite the heavy shelling and aerial bombardment there
was no change in the pisition of the Chinese defences in and
around the North Station at 6 a.m. February 6.

No further reports have been received of shells or bombs
dropping in the district.

Casualties:- Nil.
Missing:- None reported.

敬启者，
对北站附近中国军队阵地的炮击在2月13日全天断断续续持续至晚上11时30分。上午8时至9时之间，八架日本飞机协助进行轰炸，这些飞机似乎将轰炸重点集中在马克姆路（Markham Road）车站方向。它们投下了约十五枚炸弹，其爆炸声比此前听到的都要响亮得多。由于轰炸，引发了数起火灾，整个夜晚都可以看到北站在西北方向的大片区域火光冲天。

尽管遭受猛烈炮击和空中轰炸，但在2月6日上午6时，北站及其周边的中国防御阵地位置并未发生变化。（注：原文此处日期“February 6”疑为笔误，结合上下文应为2月14日或13日，但依要求照实译出）

Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by W Robertson Insp.

Sir,
During the four hour truce between the Japanese and Chinese Forces arranged from 8 a.m. till 12 noon February 12, the side gates at the Kaifeng and North Thibet Road barriers were opened by the military and a number of refugees from Chapel were allowed to enter the Settlement. Large numbers of former Chapel residents also took the opportunity to make a return visit to their homes.
At 7.45 p.m. rifle and machine gun fire accompanied by a heavy artillery bombardment broke out in the vicinity of Paoshan Road at the rear of the North Station. This continued with intensity until 11.30 p.m. when it died down somewhat and only occasional bursts of machine gun fire were heard during the night.
At 6 a.m. February 13, Chinese troops were still in possession of the North Station and their defensive positions remain unchanged.
Casualties. Nil.
Missing. None reported.

D. S. I.

D.D.O. "C"

O. i/c, Special Branch.

Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by W Robertson Insp.

Sir,
At 9 a.m. February 10, three Japanese land bombing planes
accompanied by two Scout machines appeared over Chapei and
commenced bombing in the vicinity of the North Stn. continuing
at intervals for about 2 hours. At 4.15 p.m. the aerial
bombardment of the same area was resumed by six bombing planes
and on this occasion incendiary bombs were seen to be used. At
7.15 p.m. Japanese artillery commenced to shell the same sector
and this continued with intensity until about 8.45 p.m. During
the latter bombardment a fire was seen to breakout immediately
behind the North Stn. compound near Paoshan Road in wooden
structures where it is believed Chinese troops are housed. The
fire spread rapidly to adjacent buildings and burned throughout
the night.
At 6 a.m. February 11, Chinese troops were still in
possession of the North Station and their positions remain
relatively unchanged despite the heavy aerial and artillery
bombardment during the previous day and the close proximity of
the fire.
No reports have been received of shells or bombs dropping
in the district.
Casualties. Nil.
Missing. None reported.

D. S. I.

D.D.O. "C"
O. i/c, Special Branch.

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation and State of District.

Made by D.S.I. Cash. Forwarded by W Robertson S.J.

Sir,
Commencing at 10.30 a.m. February 8, and throughout the day until 3 a.m. Feb. 9, the shelling of the North Station and Paoshan Road area by heavy artillery continued intermittently. From points of vantage near Boundary Road fresh outbreaks of fire were seen in some of the remaining buildings in Chapei as the result of the bombardment. At 7.15 p.m. Feb. 8, intensive machine gun, trench mortar and rifle fire broke out in the vicinity of the North Station and Paoshan Road. This continued until 8 p.m. when it died down somewhat and remained comparatively quiet during the night.

During the bombardment in the afternoon several shells were heard to pass over the West Hongkew Police Station coming from a northerly direction. As a result, reports were received of four shells which dropped in the district, all of which however, failed to explode. Particulars as follows:-

At 1.20 p.m. The Tz Nyi ( 主 義 ) Tobacco Factory, No.716 North Chekiang Road, owned by Huang Wei Yuen ( 洪 惠 源 ), slight damage to roof, window and first floor. Shell came to rest on ground and was brought to this Station and detained.

At 1.30 p.m. vacated house No. 3 Alabaster Road, Tenant at present unknown. Shell entered gable of house facing North. Damage unknown. Efforts are being made to locate the tenant or landlord.

At 1.30 p.m. Chinese Public Lavatory situated on the north side of Moone Road between North Honan and North Hokien Roads. Slight damage to outer wall and inside plaster. Shell fell into roadway and picked up by a member of 'A' Coy S.V.C. and taken to their H.q.

(批：Recorded)

主题（全称）紧急状态 - 每日观察及辖区状况。

由副督察长卡什（Cash）呈报。经罗伯逊（W Robertson）高级警佐转呈。

敬启者，
从2月8日上午10时30分开始，贯穿全天直至2月9日凌晨3时，重炮对北站和宝山路地区的炮击断断续续持续。从界路（Boundary Road）附近的有利观测点可以看到，由于轰炸，闸北一些残存建筑物中再次发生火灾。2月8日晚上7时15分，北站和宝山路附近爆发了激烈的机枪、迫击炮和步枪射击。这种情况一直持续到晚上8时，随后稍有减弱，夜间保持相对平静。

在下午的轰炸期间，听到数枚炮弹从北方飞来，越过西虹口巡捕房上空。因此，收到四枚炮弹落入本辖区的报告，但这四枚炮弹均未爆炸。详情如下：

下午1时20分。位于浙江北路716号的“主义”烟草厂（The Tz Nyi Tobacco Factory），业主洪惠源（Huang Wei Yuen）。屋顶、窗户和二楼轻微受损。炮弹落地静止，已被带至本巡捕房并暂存。

下午1时30分。阿拉巴斯特路（Alabaster Road）3号空置房屋，当前租户不明。炮弹击中朝北的山墙。损坏情况不明。正在努力寻找租户或房东。

下午1时30分。位于河南北路与福建北路之间慕尔路（Moone Road）北侧的中国公共厕所。外墙和内部灰泥轻微受损。炮弹落入路面，由义勇军“A”连一名成员拾起，并送往其总部。

(批：已记录)

Date 8th February 1932.

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation and State of District.

Made by D. S. I. Gash. Forwarded by

Sir,
Intermittent shelling of the North Station area by Japanese artillery continued throughout the day. The detonations were louder than have been heard hitherto, leading to the belief that heavier guns are being used. Several Japanese aircraft assisted in the bombardment between 10.30 a.m. and 1 p.m. These appeared to concentrate their bombing on the Chinese positions along Paoshan Road at the rear of the North Station. As a result, the Chinese military barracks situated behind the Station building were seen to be on fire and continued to burn during the night. At 6 a.m. February 8, despite the bombardment and occasional rifle and machine gun/fire throughout the night, the positions of the Chinese defences in the vicinity of the North Station compound were relatively unchanged.

Chinese residents throughout the district continued to vacate their homes and were seen to proceed to the more central districts.

Influx of Refugees. Some 1,400 refugees admitted through the various boundary gates which were opened by the S. V. C. during the day.

Casualties. Reported - Nil.

Missing. No reports of persons missing have been made since January 28.

D. S. I.

D. D. C. "C"
O. i/c, Special Branch.

Sir,
Commencing at about 9 a.m. February 6, and throughout the day until 5.15 p.m. the shelling of the North Station and Paoshan Road area by both Japanese and Chinese artillery continued with intensity. Between 11 a.m. and 12 noon and during the afternoon between 2.30 p.m. and 4 p.m. the Japanese bombardment was assisted by their aircraft which concentrated its bombing and machine gun fire on the Chinese positions principally at the north of the Railway Station building and along Paoshan Road. At 4.30 p.m. during the continuous bombardment of that area a shell, believed to have come from the direction of the Japanese lines, dropped in the centre of the compound of West Hongkew Police Station about midway between the Charge-Room and the foreign quarters block which faces the entrance, but failed to explode. After ricocheting off the surface the shell struck the wall of the detective office and came to rest near the steps leading to the Charge Room. The shell is similar to that of a British 13 pounder and bears the character ( カ ) believed to be Japanese, and figures 194, on the base. There were no injuries.

At the same time another projectile of the same calibre and coming from the same direction crashed through the first floor back room of a Chinese dwelling house situated at No. 120 Ching Tang Li (慶長里) about 25 yards on the north side of Elgin Road. The shell penetrated the window and wooden partition of the room and demolishing the bedstead and other pieces of furniture landed on the floor. This also failed to explode. This room was unoccupied at the time and no injuries have been reported. This shell bears the character ( 大 ) and '120' on

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation and State of District.

Sir,
Shelling in the vicinity of the North Station was continued throughout the day with intensity. The bombardment of this area and the exchange of fire commenced at 9 a.m. and continued until 5 p.m. The Japanese being assisted by aircraft which bombed and fired on essential Chinese positions. Fires were still to be seen burning throughout the night over a large area a little to the north of the Railway Station compound. Despite the heavy shelling and aerial bombardment there was no change in the position of the Chinese defences in and around the North Station at 6 a.m. February 6.

Influx of Refugees. In consequence of the complete wiring of the south side of the North Soochow Road and Police Patrol, refugees coming down the Soochow Creek were prevented from landing in West Hongkew district. Neither are there any refugees reported residing in this district.

Exodus Chinese residents throughout the district, particularly those residing north of Haining Road continued to vacate their homes, and were seen throughout the day proceeding to more central districts. Shipping Companies on North Soochow Road have suspended the issue of passage tickets for the time being due to existing conditions. It is reported that no passengers left by boat from this district and would - be travellers are being referred to the Bund offices.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
West Hongkew Station,
REPORT
Date Feb. 5th 1932.

Subject (in full) State of Emergency - Daily Observation and State of District.

Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by W Robertson Insp

Sir,
In consequence of current rumours that hostilities
would be resumed on a greater scale in the vicinity of the North
Station, the exodus of Chinese residents from this district con-
tinued throughout the day, February 4.

As a result of the completion of barbed wire defences
erected on the south side of North Soochow Road and its entire length,
the departure of river launches from jetties, this side of the
Soochow Creek has been suspended. Likewise the influx of
refugees coming down the creek who had hither-to landed at these
jetties is prevented.

Commencing at 9 a.m. and continuing throughout the day,
the vicinity of the North Station was heavily shelled by both
Chinese and Japanese artillery. At 10.40 a.m., due it is pre-
sumed to the inaccuracy of the Chinese gunners and the difficulty
in getting their range, two shells of a light gun type hit and
started a fire on the premises of a Chinese barber shop situated
at No.161 North Thibet Road. The fire spread rapidly to adjacent
buildings with result that eight adjoining Chinese shops were
practically gutted before the fire could be brought under control
by the Fire Brigade. All of these premises were vacated three
days ago and no persons have so far been reported, killed or
injured.

At the same time another shell dropped and exploded on
the roof of the General Emergency Hospital No.30 North Thibet Rd
in which premises are stationed the Portuguese and Russian
Companies S.V.C. Only slight damage was done to the building.
During subsequent enquiries it was learned that following the
explosion, a telephone message in broken English had been received

敬启者：
由于目前流传着北站附近将恢复更大规模敌对行动的谣言，2月4日全天，本区华人居民继续外迁。

由于北苏州路南侧及其全长已建成带刺铁丝网防御工事，苏州河此侧码头的内河小轮离港已暂停。同样，此前在这些码头登陆的沿河而下难民的涌入也被阻止。

自上午9时开始并持续全天，北站附近遭到中日双方炮兵的猛烈炮击。上午10时40分，据推测是由于中国炮手瞄准不准及难以测定射程，两枚轻型火炮炮弹击中并引燃了位于西藏北路161号的一家华人理发店。火势迅速蔓延至相邻建筑，导致在消防队控制火势之前，八家毗邻的华人店铺几乎被烧毁殆尽。所有这些场所已在三天前清空，截至目前尚无人员死亡或受伤的报告。

与此同时，另一枚炮弹落在西藏北路30号通用急救医院（General Emergency Hospital）的屋顶上并爆炸，葡萄牙连和俄国连的义勇军（S.V.C.）驻扎于此。建筑物仅受轻微损坏。在随后的调查中获悉，爆炸发生后，一名俄国连连队成员接到一通英语蹩脚的电话，

Date 2nd February 1932.

Subject (in full) Japanese Forces occupy a portion of Chapel -- Daily Observation
and State of District.

Made by D.S.I. Gash. Forwarded by W Robertson Insp.

Sir,
The exodus of Chinese residents from the portion of the
Settlement North of Haining Road between North Honan and North
Chekiang Roads continued throughout the day February 1. In
consequence of the recent erection of barbed wire defences on
the north side of Elgin Road and its entire length, few houses
now remain occupied in the sector between that road and the
Settlement boundary.

Upwards of 3,000 refugees coming down the Soochow Creek
landed in this district at jetties between Thibet Road and
Chekiang Road bridges. The majority of these were seen to
proceed to Central and Louza districts.

Observation was maintained in the vicinity of the North
Station where, since 10 a.m. February 1, only occasional rifle,
and machine gun fire has been heard. At 6 a.m. Feb. 2, there
was no change in the position of the Chinese defences.

No casualties were reported during the day.

(批：Recorded H.R. 2/2)

D. S. I.
D. D. O. "C"
O. i/c, Special Branch,

全天都有难民（超过3000人）从西部地区沿苏州河而下，继续在本辖区内西藏路桥以南的码头登陆，并经由浙江路和福建路桥前往老闸和中区捕房辖区。
本辖区的道路在下午6时30分后陷入黑暗，整夜几乎空无一人。
继中日双方达成停战协议后，1月31日晚上11时50分，宝山路附近爆发了激烈枪战。原因可能是日军重新占领了他们昨天撤退的宝山路东侧阵地。枪战在2月1日凌晨12时30分平息，但在夜间仍间歇性可闻。上午6时，双方部队的防御阵地均无变化。从靠近界路的有利观测点，可以看到中国援军和物资正从北站建筑废墟后方运送上来。防守该区域的中国军队极大地改善了他们的防御工事。
当日报告有一例伤亡：
一名名叫罗荣（Loo Yoong）的中国男子，30岁，广东籍，木匠，居住在海宁路旁康义里（Kong Yih Li）7号，于1月31日下午2时被流弹击中腹部受伤。

（批注：2月9日收到。WR）

File No. ______

REPORT
W. Hongkew Station,
Date 31st January 1932.

Subject (in full) Japanese Forces occupy a portion of Chapei -- Daily observation
and state of District.

Made by D.S.I. Cash. Forwarded by W.R. Robertson Insp.

Sir,
Following a night of intensive firing centered around the
Shanghai North Station which was kept up until 9 a.m. January
30, a general exodus of Chinese families residing in the portion
of the Settlement East of Elgin Road between North Honan and
North Chekiang Roads, commenced soon after dawn and continued
throughout the day. By evening dwelling houses and shops in
that area were almost entirely evacuated. This also applies in
a lesser degree to that section of the district which lies North
of Haining Road. The majority of these refugees proceeded by
way of Chekiang, Honan and Thibet Road Bridges to Central and
Louza districts and also to the French Concession where the
greater number of them are living in Hotels and lodging houses.
During the morning and early afternoon large numbers of
refugees (upwards of 2,000) coming down the Soochow Creek from
the western area, landed at jetties in this district South of
Thibet Road bridge. It was learned that they intended to re-
main in this locality for protection but later when mingling with
the general exodus from the Northern Section of this district,
they joined in with them and proceeded to the more Central
districts. By 8 p.m. the section of the district North of
Haining Road was deserted and the remainder very quiet and re-
mained so throughout the night.
Observation was maintained in the vicinity of the North
Station where there has been a lull in the firing since 9 a.m.
January 30, due it is reported, to the retreat of the Japanese
from the Szechuen Road area. The Chinese troops defending the
railway station compound have apparently been reinforced and have
also strengthened their sand bag defences.

（左侧批注：Correct / 31/1）
（左下角批注：R. / 31/1/32 / WA / [签名]）

日期 1932年1月31日。

主题（全称）日军占领闸北部分地区——日常观察及辖区状况。

制作人 副督察长 Cash。转呈人 W.R. Robertson 巡官。

先生，
在围绕上海北站进行的激烈枪战持续至1月30日上午9时之后，居住在河南路与浙江路之间、爱而近路（Elgin Road）以东的租界区域内的中国家庭，于黎明后不久开始大规模撤离，并持续了一整天。到傍晚时分，该区域的住宅和商铺几乎全部清空。海宁路以北的辖区部分也出现了程度较轻的类似情况。这些难民中的大多数人经由浙江路、河南路和西藏路桥前往中区及老闸区，也有许多人前往法租界，其中大部分人居住在旅馆和寄宿房屋中。
上午及午后早些时候，大量难民（超过2,000人）从西部区域沿苏州河而下，在西藏路桥以南的本辖区码头登陆。据悉他们打算留在此地寻求庇护，但后来当他们与本辖区北部的大规模撤离人群汇合后，便随同这些人一起前往更中心的地带。截至晚上8点，海宁路以北的辖区部分已空无一人，其余地区非常安静，并保持这种状态直至夜间结束。
在北站附近保持了观察，据报道，由于日军从四川路区域撤退，自1月30日上午9时起，该处的枪声已暂时平息。防守火车站院内的中国军队显然得到了增援，并加强了沙袋防御工事。

（左侧批注：正确 / 1月31日）
（左下角批注：R. / 1932年1月31日 / WA / [签名]）

W. Hongkew Station,
Date 30th January 19 32.
Subject (in full) Japanese Forces occupy a portion of Chapei --- Observations.
Made by D.S.I. Cash. Forwarded by W Robertson Insp
Sir,
As the result of Japanese occupation of a portion of Chinese
territory bordering Paoshan Road, military activity shortly after
4.30 a.m. January 29 centered around the Shanghai North Station
which was subjected to a heavy bombing attack from Japanese air-
craft.
Several bombs were dropped on the railway track some distance
from the station but others fell in the adjacent district in the
vicinity of Paoshan Road and started a number of fires which
spread rapidly.
At 1.20 p.m. as the result of continued aerial bombardment by
Japanese sea planes, a direct hit was made, apparently with an
incendiary bomb, on the North wing of the station building which
caught fire. Spreading rapidly the main building was soon well
alight with the result that at 9 p.m. the whole structure was
practically gutted. Sparks and burning fragments later at about
10.30 p.m. set fire to the adjacent station godown which quickly
burned and was also gutted.
The aerial bombardment ceased at dusk but rifle, machine gun
and light field gun fire continued throughout the night, with
intensity.
The small body of well equipped Chinese troops of the 19th
Div. defending the station, were still in possession at 6 a.m.
this morning January 30.
As the result of stray bullets two casualties were reported
in the district during the day. Both were pedestrians and were
wounded simultaneously at the corner of Haining and North Honan
at 2.30 p.m.
Roads. Their particulars are as follows:-

制作人 副督察长 Cash。转呈人 W Robertson 巡官
先生，
由于日军占领了毗邻宝山路的部分中国领土，军事活动于1月29日凌晨4时30分过后不久集中在上海北站周围，该站遭受了日本飞机的猛烈轰炸。
几枚炸弹投落在距离车站一定距离的铁轨上，但其他炸弹落在宝山路附近的相邻区域，引发了多起火灾并迅速蔓延。
下午1时20分，由于日本水上飞机持续的空中轰炸，车站大楼北翼被直接击中，据推测是一枚燃烧弹，导致起火。火势迅速蔓延，主楼很快烈火熊熊，结果到了晚上9点，整个建筑几乎被烧毁殆尽。随后在晚上10时30分左右，火花和燃烧的碎片引燃了相邻的车站仓库，仓库迅速燃烧并被彻底烧毁。
空中轰炸在黄昏时停止，但步枪、机枪和轻型野战炮的射击整夜持续，且强度很大。
防守车站的第19师的一小支装备精良的中国军队，直到今天（1月30日）早上6时仍控制着车站。
由于流弹，当天辖区内报告了两起伤亡事件。两人均为行人，于下午2时30分在海宁路与北河南路的拐角处同时受伤。
他们的具体情况如下：-
余秋生 (Tse Tshou Sung)，36岁，宁波人，校对员，文盲。

West Hongkew Station,
REPORT
Date January 29th 19 32
Subject (in full) Seizure of 2 Mauser Pistols, 4 wooden holsters, 1 leather holster
4 ammunition belts, and 833 rounds of 7.63 Mauser ammunition.
Made by D.P.S. Houghton. Forwarded by W.R. Robertson Insp.
Sir,
At 8:30pm. 29-1-32, 2 Chinese Railway Policemen, named Zau Tuh
Loong, and Tsang Nyoch Ding, respectively, reported at this station
that about 1pm. this date they had deserted the S.N.R. Station,
and made their way to the Settlement, through the garage of the
China Transportation Co. Boundary Road. On their arrival at the
garage they deposited 4 Mauser pistols, 4 wooden holsters, 1 leath-
er holster, 4 Ammunition belts, and a quantity of ammunition, which
they had brought with them from the railway station. Leaving this
in the care of the accountant of the firm, they left the premises
to visit friends in the Kaifeng Road district.
They now requested that this property should be recovered, and
detained at this station pending a return to normal conditions,
when an application for its return would be made by their employers
The undersigned T.S. Cox and C.D.C. 308 accompanied by these two
men proceeded to the above garage, and there recovered 2 9mm. cal.
Mauser pistols, 4 wooden holsters, 1 leather holster, 4 ammunition
belts, and 833 rounds of Mauser ammunition, which was brought to
the station, and is at present detained here.
At the time of detectives visit a coolie was the only person
present on the premises, and he stated that he was unaware of the
number of pistols deposited by the informants, and that owing to
the prevailing conditions the accountant who generally resides on
the premises had left about 2 pm. this date for a destination un-
known to him, but he was unable to state whether or not this man
had taken the other two pistols with him. A search was made of the
premises but no trace of these pistols could be found. A further
visit will be made to the premises on 30-1-32 with a view to ques-
tioning the accountant, or obtaining information that would assist
in locating him however, and any information to hand will be re-
ported
I am, Sir,
J. Houghton
D.P.S.

报告

主题（全称）查获2支毛瑟手枪、4个木质枪套、1个皮质枪套、4条弹药带及833发7.63毫米毛瑟子弹。
制作人 侦探副巡官 Houghton。转呈人 W.R. Robertson 巡官。
先生，
1932年1月29日晚上8时30分，两名名为赵土龙 (Zau Tuh Loong) 和曾耀庭 (Tsang Nyoch Ding) 的中国铁路警察来到本警署报告称，约当日下午1时，他们离开了沪宁铁路（S.N.R.）车站，穿过界路（Boundary Road）中国运输公司（China Transportation Co.）的车库进入租界。到达车库后，他们存放了4支毛瑟手枪、4个木质枪套、1个皮质枪套、4条弹药带以及一批从火车站带来的子弹。将这些物品交由该公司的会计保管后，他们离开 premises 去开封路地区拜访朋友。
他们现在请求追回这些财物，并在局势恢复正常之前将其扣押在本警署，届时将由其雇主申请归还。
下述人员 T.S. Cox 和华籍侦探 308号 (C.D.C. 308) 在这两人的陪同下前往上述车库，在那里找回了2支9毫米口径毛瑟手枪、4个木质枪套、1个皮质枪套、4条弹药带和833发毛瑟子弹，这些物品已被带回警署，目前扣押于此。
在侦探访问时，现场只有一名苦力在场，他表示不知道举报人存放的手枪数量，并且由于当时的局势，通常住在该处的会计已于当日下午2时左右离开，去向不明，但他无法说明此人是否带走了另外两支手枪。对现场进行了搜查，但未发现这些手枪的踪迹。计划于1932年1月30日再次访问该处，以便讯问会计或获取有助于找到他的信息，然而，任何到手的信息都将予以报告。
此致，
J. Houghton
侦探副巡官 (D.P.S.)
